Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾" [[Also narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (4341) from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad ibn Sinan, both from Abu Mu'awiyah. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/327): "This is a sound chain according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs."]].

Ibn Juraij said, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: "No servant is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling in Paradise is built and his dwelling in the Fire is demolished; as for the disbeliever, his dwelling in Paradise is demolished and his dwelling in the Fire is built." Something similar was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Thus the believers inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, because they were all created to worship Allah alone without partner. When these believers fulfilled what was obligatory upon them of worship, and those others neglected what they were commanded and for which they were created, these obtained the share that those would have had had they obeyed their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Even more eloquent than this is what is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection some Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them and place them upon the Jews and Christians" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]].

In another wording of his: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'" Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz then made Abu Burdah swear by Allah, besides whom there is no god, three times, that his father had narrated this to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]]

I say: this verse is like His saying: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from among Our servants whoever was righteous﴾ [Maryam: 63], and like His saying: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72]. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Al-Jannah in Roman (Greek) is al-Firdaws."

Some of the early scholars said: "A garden is not called firdaws unless it contains grapevines." And Allah knows best.

**Commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun (Chapter 23)**

Tafsir of Surat al-Mu'minun [[In MS F: "al-Mu'minin".]]
Meccan.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Yunus ibn Sulaym informed me, and Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli [[In MS A: "Zayd".]] dictated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a sound like the buzzing of bees could be heard near his face. We waited for a while. Then he faced the qiblah, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us; honour us and do not humiliate us; give to us and do not deprive us; prefer us and do not prefer others over us; be pleased with us and make us pleased [[The phrase "be pleased with us" is an addition from MS F, MS A and the Musnad.]]." Then he said: "Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever observes them will enter Paradise." Then he recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾, until he finished the ten.

This was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and by al-Nasa'i in (the book) al-Salah, from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq with this chain [[Musnad (1/34), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3173), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (1439).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: It is munkar (rejected); we know of no one who narrated it except Yunus ibn Sulaym, and we do not know Yunus.

Al-Nasa'i said in his Tafsir: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Imran, from Yazid ibn Babanus, who said: We asked Aishah: "O Mother of the Believers, what was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "The character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur'an." Then she recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ until she reached: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, and she said: "This was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11350).]].

It has been narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah and others: When Allah created the Garden of Eden and planted it with His hand, He looked at it and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: [it said this] because of the honour He had prepared for them therein. Abu al-Aliyah said: Then Allah revealed that in His Book.

This has also been narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) form. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Salamah narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and planted it, and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels entered it and said: "Good tidings to you, abode of kings!" [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3507), Kashf al-Astar. Note: the chain of Musnad al-Bazzar appears as: "Hadathana Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, hadathana Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, hadathana Hammad ibn Salamah, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id."]]

Then he said [[In MS A: "And he said".]]: And Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, and Yunus ibn Ubayd Allah al-Umari narrated to us, Adi ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk." Abu Bakr said: I saw in another place in this hadith: "The wall of Paradise: one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels said: 'Good tidings to you, abode of kings!'"

Then al-Bazzar said: We know of no one who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ) except Adi ibn al-Fadl, and he is not a hafiz (memoriser of hadith); he is an old shaykh of advanced age. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3508), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/397): "The men of the mawquf (the version ending with a Companion) are the men of the Sahih."]]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, and no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/184).]]."

Baqiyyah: his narrations from the Hijazis are weak.

Al-Tabarani also said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Hammad ibn Isa al-Absi narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "When Allah created the Garden of Eden with His hand, and hung its fruits, and split its rivers, then He looked at it and said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾." He said: "By My might, no miser shall be my neighbour in it" [[In MS A: "By My might and My majesty".]] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4861), Majma' al-Bahrayn. Abu Salih is weak.]].

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Bazzar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi narrated to us, Ya'ish ibn Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah created the Garden of Eden with His hand: one brick of white pearl, one brick of red ruby, one brick of green emerald; its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls, and its grass is saffron. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said [[In MS A: "Then it said".]]: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then Allah said: 'By My might and My majesty, no miser shall be my neighbour in you.'" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9] [[Sifat al-Jannah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya no. (20). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Note: in Sifat al-Jannah the chain reads: "Hadathana Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi, hadathana Bishr ibn al-Husayn." In al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim of Ibn Kathir (2/279) it reads: "Nufays ibn Diyn."]].

So the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ means: they have won, been made happy, and attained success, and they are the believers who possess these qualities.

﴿Those who are humble in their prayer﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿khashi'un (humble)﴾: "fearful and still." The same was narrated from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Zuhri [[In MS F and MS A: "al-Zuhri and Qatadah".]].

And from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: "Khushu' is the humility of the heart." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i also said the same.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze because of it, and lowered their wings (in humility).

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise their gaze to the sky during prayer. When this verse was revealed: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded. Those who are humble in their prayer﴾, they lowered their gaze to the place of their prostration.

[And] [[Addition from MS A.]] Ibn Sirin said: They used to say: "One's gaze should not go beyond his prayer place; if one is accustomed to looking around, let him close his eyes." Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated from him, and also from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, as a mursal (a report with a missing Companion), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do this until this verse was revealed [[In MS A: "And he narrated".]].

Humility in prayer is only attained by one who empties his heart for it, is occupied with it to the exclusion of all else, prefers it over other things; and then it becomes a comfort and a delight for him, as the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith which Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Perfume and women have been made beloved to me, and the coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer" [[Musnad (3/128) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6117).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from a man of Aslam, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Bilal, give us rest with the prayer" [[Musnad (5/364).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: I entered with my father upon a relative of ours from the Ansar. The prayer time came, and he said: "O girl, bring me water for ablution, so that I may pray and rest." He saw that we disapproved of this, so he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Stand, O Bilal, and give us rest with the prayer'" [[In MS F and MS A: "He saw us disapproving of that from him".]] [[Musnad (5/371).]].

And (Allah) said: ﴿And those who turn away from vain talk﴾, meaning: from falsehood. This includes shirk, as some of them said; and sins, as others said; and whatever has no benefit in it of words and deeds, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

Qatadah said: "By Allah, there came to them from the command of Allah something that deterred them from that."
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who are active in giving zakah﴾. Most scholars hold that what is meant by zakah here is zakat al-amwal (the zakah on wealth), although this verse is Meccan; zakah was prescribed in Medina in the second year after the Hijrah. The apparent meaning is that what was prescribed in Medina was the one with its specific nisab (threshold) and amounts; otherwise the apparent meaning is that the basis of zakah was obligatory in Mecca, as Allah, the Exalted, said in Surat al-An'am, which is Meccan: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ [al-An'am: 141].

It is also possible that what is meant by zakah here is the purification of the soul from shirk and impurity, as in His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 9–10], and as in His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah﴾ [Fussilat: 6–7], according to one of the two opinions regarding its interpretation.

It is also possible that both are intended: purification of the souls and zakah of wealth, for it is part of the purification of the souls. The complete believer is one who engages in both. And Allah knows best.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾. Meaning: those who have guarded their private parts from what is unlawful, so they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them, such as fornication or sodomy; and they approach none but their wives, whom Allah has made lawful to them, and what their right hands possess of concubines. Whoever engages in what Allah has made lawful for him, there is no blame upon him and no sin. For this reason He said: ﴿for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that﴾, meaning: beyond wives and slave-girls, ﴿it is those who are the transgressors﴾, meaning: the aggressors.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that a woman took her male slave as a lover, and said: "I interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾." So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some men among the Companions of the Prophet [[In MS A: "Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ said to him: "She interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah in other than its proper sense." He said: "So he struck the slave and cut off his head," and said: "You are, after him, unlawful to every Muslim." This is a strange and broken (munqati') report. Ibn Jarir mentioned it at the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/586), ed. al-Ma'arif.]], and it is more fitting here. He forbade her to men only as a recompense for her, by treating her opposite to her intention. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim on surah 23, verses 1–11 (part 2 of 2):

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, used this noble verse as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation by hand: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess﴾. He said: this act falls outside these two categories, and He has said: ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, they are the transgressors﴾. They also relied on a hadith narrated by Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah in his well-known juz', where he said:

Ali ibn Thabit al-Jazari narrated to me, from Maslamah ibn Ja'far, from Hassan ibn Humayd [[In F and A: "Ahmad".]], from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Seven are those whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with those who do deeds, and He will cause them to enter the Fire first of those who enter, unless they repent. Whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance: the one who has intercourse with his hand [[In F and A: "The one who has intercourse with his hand."]], the one who commits sodomy and the one to whom it is done, the habitual drinker of wine [[In F and A: "The habitual drinker."]], the one who strikes his parents until they cry for help, the one who harms his neighbours until they curse him, and the one who has relations with his neighbour's wife." [[Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. (41).]]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith, and its chain contains someone who is not known, due to his obscurity. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant are observers﴾, meaning: when they are entrusted, they do not betray, but return the trust to its people; and when they make a covenant or a contract, they fulfil it. This is unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites, about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, meaning: they persevere in them at their appointed times. As Ibn Mas'ud said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is most beloved to Allah?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to one's parents." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5970) and Sahih Muslim no. (85).]]. In al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, it is narrated with the wording: "Prayer at the beginning of its time" [[Al-Mustadrak (1/188). Al-Hakim said: "This wording is authentic through the agreement of the two trustworthy narrators Bundar ibn Bashshar and al-Hasan ibn Mukram in their narration from Uthman ibn 'Amr, and it is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."]].

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said, regarding His saying ﴿those who are attentive to their prayers﴾: it means the appointed times of the prayer. Likewise said Abu al-Duha, 'Alqamah ibn Qays, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah.

Qatadah said: "at their appointed times, and their bowing and their prostration."

Allah began the mention of these praiseworthy characteristics with prayer and concluded them with prayer, which indicates its excellence, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count [your deeds]; and know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer" [[It came from the hadith of Thawban: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (277) through the chain of Sufyan from Mansur from Ibn Abi al-Ja'd from him, and in it there is a break (inqita'). And from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (278) through the chain of al-Mu'tamir from Layth from Mujahid from him, and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak. And from the hadith of Abu Umamah: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (279) through the chain of Ishaq ibn Asid from Abu Hafs al-Dimashqi from him, and al-Busiri weakened it in al-Zawa'id.]].

When Allah described them as upholding these praiseworthy qualities and righteous actions, He said: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein forever﴾.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful" [[Al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2790), (7423), from Abu Hurayrah; the author of Tuhfah did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Bukhari.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾" [[Also narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (4341) from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad ibn Sinan, both from Abu Mu'awiyah. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/327): "This is a sound chain according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs."]].

Ibn Juraij said, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: "No servant is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling in Paradise is built and his dwelling in the Fire is demolished; as for the disbeliever, his dwelling in Paradise is demolished and his dwelling in the Fire is built." Something similar was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Thus the believers inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, because they were all created to worship Allah alone without partner. When these believers fulfilled what was obligatory upon them of worship, and those others neglected what they were commanded and for which they were created, these obtained the share that those would have had had they obeyed their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Even more eloquent than this is what is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection some Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them and place them upon the Jews and Christians" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]].

In another wording of his: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'" Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz then made Abu Burdah swear by Allah, besides whom there is no god, three times, that his father had narrated this to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]]

I say: this verse is like His saying: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from among Our servants whoever was righteous﴾ [Maryam: 63], and like His saying: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72]. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Al-Jannah in Roman (Greek) is al-Firdaws."

Some of the early scholars said: "A garden is not called firdaws unless it contains grapevines." And Allah knows best.

**Commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun (Chapter 23)**

Tafsir of Surat al-Mu'minun [[In MS F: "al-Mu'minin".]]
Meccan.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Yunus ibn Sulaym informed me, and Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli [[In MS A: "Zayd".]] dictated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a sound like the buzzing of bees could be heard near his face. We waited for a while. Then he faced the qiblah, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us; honour us and do not humiliate us; give to us and do not deprive us; prefer us and do not prefer others over us; be pleased with us and make us pleased [[The phrase "be pleased with us" is an addition from MS F, MS A and the Musnad.]]." Then he said: "Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever observes them will enter Paradise." Then he recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾, until he finished the ten.

This was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and by al-Nasa'i in (the book) al-Salah, from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq with this chain [[Musnad (1/34), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3173), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (1439).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: It is munkar (rejected); we know of no one who narrated it except Yunus ibn Sulaym, and we do not know Yunus.

Al-Nasa'i said in his Tafsir: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Imran, from Yazid ibn Babanus, who said: We asked Aishah: "O Mother of the Believers, what was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "The character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur'an." Then she recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ until she reached: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, and she said: "This was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11350).]].

It has been narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah and others: When Allah created the Garden of Eden and planted it with His hand, He looked at it and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: [it said this] because of the honour He had prepared for them therein. Abu al-Aliyah said: Then Allah revealed that in His Book.

This has also been narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) form. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Salamah narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and planted it, and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels entered it and said: "Good tidings to you, abode of kings!" [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3507), Kashf al-Astar. Note: the chain of Musnad al-Bazzar appears as: "Hadathana Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, hadathana Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, hadathana Hammad ibn Salamah, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id."]]

Then he said [[In MS A: "And he said".]]: And Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, and Yunus ibn Ubayd Allah al-Umari narrated to us, Adi ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk." Abu Bakr said: I saw in another place in this hadith: "The wall of Paradise: one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels said: 'Good tidings to you, abode of kings!'"

Then al-Bazzar said: We know of no one who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ) except Adi ibn al-Fadl, and he is not a hafiz (memoriser of hadith); he is an old shaykh of advanced age. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3508), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/397): "The men of the mawquf (the version ending with a Companion) are the men of the Sahih."]]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, and no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/184).]]."

Baqiyyah: his narrations from the Hijazis are weak.

Al-Tabarani also said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Hammad ibn Isa al-Absi narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "When Allah created the Garden of Eden with His hand, and hung its fruits, and split its rivers, then He looked at it and said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾." He said: "By My might, no miser shall be my neighbour in it" [[In MS A: "By My might and My majesty".]] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4861), Majma' al-Bahrayn. Abu Salih is weak.]].

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Bazzar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi narrated to us, Ya'ish ibn Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah created the Garden of Eden with His hand: one brick of white pearl, one brick of red ruby, one brick of green emerald; its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls, and its grass is saffron. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said [[In MS A: "Then it said".]]: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then Allah said: 'By My might and My majesty, no miser shall be my neighbour in you.'" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9] [[Sifat al-Jannah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya no. (20). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Note: in Sifat al-Jannah the chain reads: "Hadathana Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi, hadathana Bishr ibn al-Husayn." In al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim of Ibn Kathir (2/279) it reads: "Nufays ibn Diyn."]].

So the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ means: they have won, been made happy, and attained success, and they are the believers who possess these qualities.

﴿Those who are humble in their prayer﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿khashi'un (humble)﴾: "fearful and still." The same was narrated from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Zuhri [[In MS F and MS A: "al-Zuhri and Qatadah".]].

And from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: "Khushu' is the humility of the heart." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i also said the same.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze because of it, and lowered their wings (in humility).

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise their gaze to the sky during prayer. When this verse was revealed: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded. Those who are humble in their prayer﴾, they lowered their gaze to the place of their prostration.

[And] [[Addition from MS A.]] Ibn Sirin said: They used to say: "One's gaze should not go beyond his prayer place; if one is accustomed to looking around, let him close his eyes." Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated from him, and also from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, as a mursal (a report with a missing Companion), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do this until this verse was revealed [[In MS A: "And he narrated".]].

Humility in prayer is only attained by one who empties his heart for it, is occupied with it to the exclusion of all else, prefers it over other things; and then it becomes a comfort and a delight for him, as the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith which Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Perfume and women have been made beloved to me, and the coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer" [[Musnad (3/128) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6117).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from a man of Aslam, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Bilal, give us rest with the prayer" [[Musnad (5/364).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: I entered with my father upon a relative of ours from the Ansar. The prayer time came, and he said: "O girl, bring me water for ablution, so that I may pray and rest." He saw that we disapproved of this, so he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Stand, O Bilal, and give us rest with the prayer'" [[In MS F and MS A: "He saw us disapproving of that from him".]] [[Musnad (5/371).]].

And (Allah) said: ﴿And those who turn away from vain talk﴾, meaning: from falsehood. This includes shirk, as some of them said; and sins, as others said; and whatever has no benefit in it of words and deeds, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

Qatadah said: "By Allah, there came to them from the command of Allah something that deterred them from that."
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who are active in giving zakah﴾. Most scholars hold that what is meant by zakah here is zakat al-amwal (the zakah on wealth), although this verse is Meccan; zakah was prescribed in Medina in the second year after the Hijrah. The apparent meaning is that what was prescribed in Medina was the one with its specific nisab (threshold) and amounts; otherwise the apparent meaning is that the basis of zakah was obligatory in Mecca, as Allah, the Exalted, said in Surat al-An'am, which is Meccan: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ [al-An'am: 141].

It is also possible that what is meant by zakah here is the purification of the soul from shirk and impurity, as in His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 9–10], and as in His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah﴾ [Fussilat: 6–7], according to one of the two opinions regarding its interpretation.

It is also possible that both are intended: purification of the souls and zakah of wealth, for it is part of the purification of the souls. The complete believer is one who engages in both. And Allah knows best.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾. Meaning: those who have guarded their private parts from what is unlawful, so they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them, such as fornication or sodomy; and they approach none but their wives, whom Allah has made lawful to them, and what their right hands possess of concubines. Whoever engages in what Allah has made lawful for him, there is no blame upon him and no sin. For this reason He said: ﴿for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that﴾, meaning: beyond wives and slave-girls, ﴿it is those who are the transgressors﴾, meaning: the aggressors.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that a woman took her male slave as a lover, and said: "I interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾." So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some men among the Companions of the Prophet [[In MS A: "Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ said to him: "She interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah in other than its proper sense." He said: "So he struck the slave and cut off his head," and said: "You are, after him, unlawful to every Muslim." This is a strange and broken (munqati') report. Ibn Jarir mentioned it at the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/586), ed. al-Ma'arif.]], and it is more fitting here. He forbade her to men only as a recompense for her, by treating her opposite to her intention. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim on surah 23, verses 1–11 (part 2 of 2):

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, used this noble verse as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation by hand: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess﴾. He said: this act falls outside these two categories, and He has said: ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, they are the transgressors﴾. They also relied on a hadith narrated by Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah in his well-known juz', where he said:

Ali ibn Thabit al-Jazari narrated to me, from Maslamah ibn Ja'far, from Hassan ibn Humayd [[In F and A: "Ahmad".]], from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Seven are those whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with those who do deeds, and He will cause them to enter the Fire first of those who enter, unless they repent. Whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance: the one who has intercourse with his hand [[In F and A: "The one who has intercourse with his hand."]], the one who commits sodomy and the one to whom it is done, the habitual drinker of wine [[In F and A: "The habitual drinker."]], the one who strikes his parents until they cry for help, the one who harms his neighbours until they curse him, and the one who has relations with his neighbour's wife." [[Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. (41).]]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith, and its chain contains someone who is not known, due to his obscurity. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant are observers﴾, meaning: when they are entrusted, they do not betray, but return the trust to its people; and when they make a covenant or a contract, they fulfil it. This is unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites, about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, meaning: they persevere in them at their appointed times. As Ibn Mas'ud said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is most beloved to Allah?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to one's parents." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5970) and Sahih Muslim no. (85).]]. In al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, it is narrated with the wording: "Prayer at the beginning of its time" [[Al-Mustadrak (1/188). Al-Hakim said: "This wording is authentic through the agreement of the two trustworthy narrators Bundar ibn Bashshar and al-Hasan ibn Mukram in their narration from Uthman ibn 'Amr, and it is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."]].

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said, regarding His saying ﴿those who are attentive to their prayers﴾: it means the appointed times of the prayer. Likewise said Abu al-Duha, 'Alqamah ibn Qays, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah.

Qatadah said: "at their appointed times, and their bowing and their prostration."

Allah began the mention of these praiseworthy characteristics with prayer and concluded them with prayer, which indicates its excellence, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count [your deeds]; and know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer" [[It came from the hadith of Thawban: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (277) through the chain of Sufyan from Mansur from Ibn Abi al-Ja'd from him, and in it there is a break (inqita'). And from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (278) through the chain of al-Mu'tamir from Layth from Mujahid from him, and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak. And from the hadith of Abu Umamah: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (279) through the chain of Ishaq ibn Asid from Abu Hafs al-Dimashqi from him, and al-Busiri weakened it in al-Zawa'id.]].

When Allah described them as upholding these praiseworthy qualities and righteous actions, He said: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein forever﴾.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful" [[Al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2790), (7423), from Abu Hurayrah; the author of Tuhfah did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Bukhari.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾" [[Also narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (4341) from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad ibn Sinan, both from Abu Mu'awiyah. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/327): "This is a sound chain according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs."]].

Ibn Juraij said, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: "No servant is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling in Paradise is built and his dwelling in the Fire is demolished; as for the disbeliever, his dwelling in Paradise is demolished and his dwelling in the Fire is built." Something similar was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Thus the believers inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, because they were all created to worship Allah alone without partner. When these believers fulfilled what was obligatory upon them of worship, and those others neglected what they were commanded and for which they were created, these obtained the share that those would have had had they obeyed their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Even more eloquent than this is what is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection some Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them and place them upon the Jews and Christians" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]].

In another wording of his: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'" Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz then made Abu Burdah swear by Allah, besides whom there is no god, three times, that his father had narrated this to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]]

I say: this verse is like His saying: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from among Our servants whoever was righteous﴾ [Maryam: 63], and like His saying: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72]. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Al-Jannah in Roman (Greek) is al-Firdaws."

Some of the early scholars said: "A garden is not called firdaws unless it contains grapevines." And Allah knows best.

**Commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun (Chapter 23)**

Tafsir of Surat al-Mu'minun [[In MS F: "al-Mu'minin".]]
Meccan.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Yunus ibn Sulaym informed me, and Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli [[In MS A: "Zayd".]] dictated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a sound like the buzzing of bees could be heard near his face. We waited for a while. Then he faced the qiblah, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us; honour us and do not humiliate us; give to us and do not deprive us; prefer us and do not prefer others over us; be pleased with us and make us pleased [[The phrase "be pleased with us" is an addition from MS F, MS A and the Musnad.]]." Then he said: "Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever observes them will enter Paradise." Then he recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾, until he finished the ten.

This was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir and by al-Nasa'i in (the book) al-Salah, from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq with this chain [[Musnad (1/34), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3173), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (1439).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: It is munkar (rejected); we know of no one who narrated it except Yunus ibn Sulaym, and we do not know Yunus.

Al-Nasa'i said in his Tafsir: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Imran, from Yazid ibn Babanus, who said: We asked Aishah: "O Mother of the Believers, what was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "The character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur'an." Then she recited: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ until she reached: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, and she said: "This was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11350).]].

It has been narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah and others: When Allah created the Garden of Eden and planted it with His hand, He looked at it and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: [it said this] because of the honour He had prepared for them therein. Abu al-Aliyah said: Then Allah revealed that in His Book.

This has also been narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) form. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Salamah narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and planted it, and said to it: "Speak." It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels entered it and said: "Good tidings to you, abode of kings!" [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3507), Kashf al-Astar. Then he said [[In MS A: "And he said".]]: And Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, and Yunus ibn Ubayd Allah al-Umari narrated to us, Adi ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Paradise, one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk." Abu Bakr said: I saw in another place in this hadith: "The wall of Paradise: one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾. Then the angels said: 'Good tidings to you, abode of kings!'"

Then al-Bazzar said: We know of no one who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ) except Adi ibn al-Fadl, and he is not a hafiz (memoriser of hadith); he is an old shaykh of advanced age. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3508), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/397): "The men of the mawquf (the version ending with a Companion) are the men of the Sahih."]]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, and no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/184).]]."

Baqiyyah: his narrations from the Hijazis are weak.

Al-Tabarani also said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Hammad ibn Isa al-Absi narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "When Allah created the Garden of Eden with His hand, and hung its fruits, and split its rivers, then He looked at it and said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾." (20). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Note: in Sifat al-Jannah the chain reads: "Hadathana Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Kalbi, hadathana Bishr ibn al-Husayn." ﴿Those who are humble in their prayer﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿khashi'un (humble)﴾: "fearful and still." The same was narrated from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Zuhri [[In MS F and MS A: "al-Zuhri and Qatadah".]].

And from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: "Khushu' is the humility of the heart." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i also said the same.

Then Ibn Jarir narrated from him, and also from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, as a mursal (a report with a missing Companion), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do this until this verse was revealed [[In MS A: "And he narrated".]].

The prayer time came, and he said: "O girl, bring me water for ablution, so that I may pray and rest." He saw that we disapproved of this, so he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Stand, O Bilal, and give us rest with the prayer'" [[In MS F and MS A: "He saw us disapproving of that from him".]] [[Musnad (5/371).]].

And (Allah) said: ﴿And those who turn away from vain talk﴾, meaning: from falsehood. This includes shirk, as some of them said; and sins, as others said; and whatever has no benefit in it of words and deeds, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

Qatadah said: "By Allah, there came to them from the command of Allah something that deterred them from that."
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who are active in giving zakah﴾. Most scholars hold that what is meant by zakah here is zakat al-amwal (the zakah on wealth), although this verse is Meccan; zakah was prescribed in Medina in the second year after the Hijrah. The apparent meaning is that what was prescribed in Medina was the one with its specific nisab (threshold) and amounts; otherwise the apparent meaning is that the basis of zakah was obligatory in Mecca, as Allah, the Exalted, said in Surat al-An'am, which is Meccan: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ [al-An'am: 141].

It is also possible that what is meant by zakah here is the purification of the soul from shirk and impurity, as in His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 9–10], and as in His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah﴾ [Fussilat: 6–7], according to one of the two opinions regarding its interpretation.

It is also possible that both are intended: purification of the souls and zakah of wealth, for it is part of the purification of the souls. The complete believer is one who engages in both. And Allah knows best.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾. Meaning: those who have guarded their private parts from what is unlawful, so they do not commit what Allah has forbidden them, such as fornication or sodomy; and they approach none but their wives, whom Allah has made lawful to them, and what their right hands possess of concubines. Whoever engages in what Allah has made lawful for him, there is no blame upon him and no sin. For this reason He said: ﴿for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that﴾, meaning: beyond wives and slave-girls, ﴿it is those who are the transgressors﴾, meaning: the aggressors.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that a woman took her male slave as a lover, and said: "I interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾." So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some men among the Companions of the Prophet [[In MS A: "Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ said to him: "She interpreted a verse from the Book of Allah in other than its proper sense." He said: "So he struck the slave and cut off his head," and said: "You are, after him, unlawful to every Muslim." This is a strange and broken (munqati') report. Ibn Jarir mentioned it at the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat al-Ma'idah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/586), ed. al-Ma'arif.]], and it is more fitting here. He forbade her to men only as a recompense for her, by treating her opposite to her intention. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim on surah 23, verses 1–11 (part 2 of 2):

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, used this noble verse as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation by hand: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess﴾. He said: this act falls outside these two categories, and He has said: ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, they are the transgressors﴾. They also relied on a hadith narrated by Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah in his well-known juz', where he said:

Ali ibn Thabit al-Jazari narrated to me, from Maslamah ibn Ja'far, from Hassan ibn Humayd [[In F and A: "Ahmad".]], from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Seven are those whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with those who do deeds, and He will cause them to enter the Fire first of those who enter, unless they repent. Whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance: the one who has intercourse with his hand [[In F and A: "The one who has intercourse with his hand."]], the one who commits sodomy and the one to whom it is done, the habitual drinker of wine [[In F and A: "The habitual drinker."]], the one who strikes his parents until they cry for help, the one who harms his neighbours until they curse him, and the one who has relations with his neighbour's wife." [[Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. (41).]]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith, and its chain contains someone who is not known, due to his obscurity. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant are observers﴾, meaning: when they are entrusted, they do not betray, but return the trust to its people; and when they make a covenant or a contract, they fulfil it. This is unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites, about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, meaning: they persevere in them at their appointed times. As Ibn Mas'ud said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is most beloved to Allah?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Kindness to one's parents." I said: "Then which?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5970) and Sahih Muslim no. (85).]]. In al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, it is narrated with the wording: "Prayer at the beginning of its time" [[Al-Mustadrak (1/188). Al-Hakim said: "This wording is authentic through the agreement of the two trustworthy narrators Bundar ibn Bashshar and al-Hasan ibn Mukram in their narration from Uthman ibn 'Amr, and it is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."]].

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said, regarding His saying ﴿those who are attentive to their prayers﴾: it means the appointed times of the prayer. Likewise said Abu al-Duha, 'Alqamah ibn Qays, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah.

Qatadah said: "at their appointed times, and their bowing and their prostration."

Allah began the mention of these praiseworthy characteristics with prayer and concluded them with prayer, which indicates its excellence, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count [your deeds]; and know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains ablution except a believer" [[It came from the hadith of Thawban: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (277) through the chain of Sufyan from Mansur from Ibn Abi al-Ja'd from him, and in it there is a break (inqita'). And from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (278) through the chain of al-Mu'tamir from Layth from Mujahid from him, and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak. And from the hadith of Abu Umamah: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (279) through the chain of Ishaq ibn Asid from Abu Hafs al-Dimashqi from him, and al-Busiri weakened it in al-Zawa'id.]].

When Allah described them as upholding these praiseworthy qualities and righteous actions, He said: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein forever﴾.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful" [[Al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2790), (7423), from Abu Hurayrah; the author of Tuhfah did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Bukhari.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾" [[Also narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (4341) from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad ibn Sinan, both from Abu Mu'awiyah. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/327): "This is a sound chain according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs."]].

Ibn Juraij said, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: "No servant is without two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling in Paradise is built and his dwelling in the Fire is demolished; as for the disbeliever, his dwelling in Paradise is demolished and his dwelling in the Fire is built." Something similar was also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Thus the believers inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, because they were all created to worship Allah alone without partner. When these believers fulfilled what was obligatory upon them of worship, and those others neglected what they were commanded and for which they were created, these obtained the share that those would have had had they obeyed their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Even more eloquent than this is what is established in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection some Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them and place them upon the Jews and Christians" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]].

In another wording of his: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'" Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz then made Abu Burdah swear by Allah, besides whom there is no god, three times, that his father had narrated this to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2767).]]

I say: this verse is like His saying: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from among Our servants whoever was righteous﴾ [Maryam: 63], and like His saying: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72]. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Al-Jannah in Roman (Greek) is al-Firdaws."

Some of the early scholars said: "A garden is not called firdaws unless it contains grapevines." And Allah knows best.

He says, informing about the beginning of the creation of man from an extract of clay, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah created him from *salsal* (dried clay that rings) of *hama'* (black, altered mud) *masnun* (molded).

Al-A'mash related from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Yahya, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿From an extract of clay﴾, he said: "The purest part of the water."

Mujahid said: ﴿From an extract﴾, meaning: from the semen of Adam.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Adam was called "clay" only because he was created from it.

Qatadah said: Adam was extracted from the clay. This is more apparent in meaning and closer to the context, for Adam, peace be upon him, was created from *tin lazib* (sticky clay), which is the *salsal* of *hama' masnun*, and that is created from dust, as Allah says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersed﴾ [al-Rum: 20].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, 'Awf related to us, Qassamah ibn Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Adam from a handful He took from all of the earth, so the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them is the red, the black, and the white, and what is between those; and the evil and the good, and what is between those."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, through several chains, from 'Awf al-A'rabi, similar to it. [Al-Musnad (4/400), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4693), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2955).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

﴿Then We made him a drop of semen﴾: This pronoun refers to the species of man, as He says in another verse: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his offspring from an extract of worthless fluid﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7-8], meaning weak, as He says: ﴿Did We not create you from a worthless fluid? And We placed it in a secure place﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20-21], meaning the womb, prepared and readied for that, ﴿for a known period﴾ [al-Mursalat: 22], and a known term, and a specified time, until it became firm and passed from one state to another and from one attribute to another. For this reason He says here: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾, meaning: then We transformed the drop, which is the gushing fluid that issues from the loins of the man, which is his back, and the breastbones of the woman, which are the bones of her chest between the collarbone and the nipple, so it became a red clinging clot, shaped like a leech, elongated. 'Ikrimah said: it is blood.

﴿Then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾: It is a piece like a morsel of flesh, having no form and no outline. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, meaning: We shaped it with a head, two hands, and two feet, with its bones, its sinews, and its veins.

Others recited: ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾ [in some readings: "the drop bones"]. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the bone of the spine.

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every part of the son of Adam decays except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reassembled."

﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, meaning: and We placed upon that what covers it, binds it, and strengthens it. ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: then We breathed the spirit into it, and it moved, and became ﴿another creation﴾, possessing hearing, sight, perception, movement, and motion. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ja'far ibn Musafir related to us, Yahya ibn Hassan related to us, al-Nadr (meaning Ibn Kathir, client of the Banu Hashim) related to us, Zayd ibn 'Ali related to us, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the drop completes four months, an angel is sent to it, and he breathes the spirit into it in the three darknesses. That is His saying: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: We breathed the spirit into it.

It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the breathing of the spirit.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning by it: the spirit. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/81).]

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: We move him from state to state, until he emerges as an infant, then grows up as a child, then reaches puberty, then becomes a youth, then a middle-aged man, then an old man, then decrepit.

Similar to this is narrated from Qatadah and al-Dahhak. There is no contradiction, for from the beginning of the breathing of the spirit into him, he began these transitions and states. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abd Allah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us, and he is the truthful and the believed: "Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for the same period, then he becomes a lump for the same period. Then the angel is sent to him, and he breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or fortunate. By He other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Book precedes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed a man may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Book precedes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash. [Al-Musnad (1/382), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6594), Sahih Muslim no. (2643).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah related to us from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, who said: 'Abd Allah (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) said: When the drop falls into the womb, it spreads into every hair and nail, then it remains for forty days, then it slides down in the womb and becomes a clot.

Imam Ahmad also said: Husayn ibn al-Hasan related to us, Abu Kudaynah related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from 'Abd Allah, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was narrating to his companions. Quraysh said: "O Jew, this man claims that he is a prophet." He said: "I will surely ask him about something that none but a prophet knows." So he came and sat down and said: "O Muhammad, from what is man created?" He said: "O Jew, from both: from the drop of the man and from the drop of the woman. As for the drop of the man, it is a thick drop from which come the bone and the sinew; and as for the drop of the woman, it is a thin drop from which come the flesh and the blood." The Jew stood up and said: "Thus used to say those before you." [Al-Musnad (1/465).]

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us from 'Amr, from Abu al-Tufayl, Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The angel enters upon the drop after it settles in the womb by forty nights, and says: 'O Lord, what? Is he wretched or fortunate? Is he male or female?' Allah decrees, and the two write. They say: 'What? Male or female?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees, and the two write, and his deeds, his traces, his calamity, and his provision are written. Then the scroll is folded, and nothing is added to what is in it nor subtracted from it."

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, that is Ibn Dinar, with the same meaning. And from other chains, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd Abu Surayhah al-Ghifari, similar to it. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. (2644), and no. (2645).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has appointed over the womb an angel who says: 'O Lord, a drop. O Lord, a clot. O Lord, a lump.' When Allah wills to create it, he says: 'O Lord, male or female? Wretched or fortunate? What is the provision and the term?'" He said: "So that is written in the belly of its mother."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (318), Sahih Muslim no. (2646).]

* *

His saying: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, meaning: when He mentioned His power and His subtle care in creating this drop from state to state and from form to form, until it took shape and became the complete, perfectly formed human being, He said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib related to us, Abu Dawud related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd related to us, from Anas, who said: 'Umar, meaning Ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I agreed with my Lord in four things: this verse was revealed: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ to the end of the verse, and I said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. Then it was revealed: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾."

He also said: My father related to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us, Shaybān related to us, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah dictated to me this verse: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ up to His saying: ﴿another creation﴾. Then Mu'adh said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed. Mu'adh said to him: "At what did you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "With it the verse was concluded: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (3367), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," from Abu Zur'ah, from Adam ibn Iyas with it; Jabir al-Ju'fi is weak.]

Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi is extremely weak, and in this report there is severe strangeness, because this sura is Meccan, Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote down the revelation in Medina, and similarly the conversion of Mu'adh ibn Jabal also took place in Medina. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then indeed you, after that, are surely dead﴾, meaning: after this first origination from non-existence, you will come to death. ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected﴾, meaning: the final origination. ﴿Then Allah originates the final creation﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 20], meaning: on the Day of Return, and the rising of the spirits and the bodies, when He will call the creation to account and repay every worker for his deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.

He says, informing about the beginning of the creation of man from an extract of clay, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah created him from *salsal* (dried clay that rings) of *hama'* (black, altered mud) *masnun* (molded).

Al-A'mash related from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Yahya, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿From an extract of clay﴾, he said: "The purest part of the water."

Mujahid said: ﴿From an extract﴾, meaning: from the semen of Adam.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Adam was called "clay" only because he was created from it.

Qatadah said: Adam was extracted from the clay. This is more apparent in meaning and closer to the context, for Adam, peace be upon him, was created from *tin lazib* (sticky clay), which is the *salsal* of *hama' masnun*, and that is created from dust, as Allah says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersed﴾ [al-Rum: 20].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, 'Awf related to us, Qassamah ibn Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Adam from a handful He took from all of the earth, so the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them is the red, the black, and the white, and what is between those; and the evil and the good, and what is between those."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, through several chains, from 'Awf al-A'rabi, similar to it. [Al-Musnad (4/400), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4693), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2955).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

﴿Then We made him a drop of semen﴾: This pronoun refers to the species of man, as He says in another verse: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his offspring from an extract of worthless fluid﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7-8], meaning weak, as He says: ﴿Did We not create you from a worthless fluid? And We placed it in a secure place﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20-21], meaning the womb, prepared and readied for that, ﴿for a known period﴾ [al-Mursalat: 22], and a known term, and a specified time, until it became firm and passed from one state to another and from one attribute to another. For this reason He says here: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾, meaning: then We transformed the drop, which is the gushing fluid that issues from the loins of the man, which is his back, and the breastbones of the woman, which are the bones of her chest between the collarbone and the nipple, so it became a red clinging clot, shaped like a leech, elongated. 'Ikrimah said: it is blood.

﴿Then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾: It is a piece like a morsel of flesh, having no form and no outline. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, meaning: We shaped it with a head, two hands, and two feet, with its bones, its sinews, and its veins.

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every part of the son of Adam decays except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reassembled."

﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, meaning: and We placed upon that what covers it, binds it, and strengthens it. ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: then We breathed the spirit into it, and it moved, and became ﴿another creation﴾, possessing hearing, sight, perception, movement, and motion. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ja'far ibn Musafir related to us, Yahya ibn Hassan related to us, al-Nadr (meaning Ibn Kathir, client of the Banu Hashim) related to us, Zayd ibn 'Ali related to us, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the drop completes four months, an angel is sent to it, and he breathes the spirit into it in the three darknesses. That is His saying: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: We breathed the spirit into it.

It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the breathing of the spirit.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning by it: the spirit. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/81).]

Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abd Allah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us, and he is the truthful and the believed: "Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for the same period, then he becomes a lump for the same period. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Adam was called "clay" only because he was created from it.

Others recited: ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾ [in some readings: "the drop bones"]. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the bone of the spine.
