He also said: My father related to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us, Shaybān related to us, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah dictated to me this verse: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ up to His saying: ﴿another creation﴾. Then Mu'adh said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed. Mu'adh said to him: "At what did you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "With it the verse was concluded: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (3367), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," from Abu Zur'ah, from Adam ibn Iyas with it; Jabir al-Ju'fi is weak.]

Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi is extremely weak, and in this report there is severe strangeness, because this sura is Meccan, Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote down the revelation in Medina, and similarly the conversion of Mu'adh ibn Jabal also took place in Medina. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then indeed you, after that, are surely dead﴾, meaning: after this first origination from non-existence, you will come to death. ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected﴾, meaning: the final origination. ﴿Then Allah originates the final creation﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 20], meaning: on the Day of Return, and the rising of the spirits and the bodies, when He will call the creation to account and repay every worker for his deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.

He says, informing about the beginning of the creation of man from an extract of clay, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah created him from *salsal* (dried clay that rings) of *hama'* (black, altered mud) *masnun* (molded).

Al-A'mash related from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Yahya, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿From an extract of clay﴾, he said: "The purest part of the water."

Mujahid said: ﴿From an extract﴾, meaning: from the semen of Adam.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Adam was called "clay" only because he was created from it.

Qatadah said: Adam was extracted from the clay. This is more apparent in meaning and closer to the context, for Adam, peace be upon him, was created from *tin lazib* (sticky clay), which is the *salsal* of *hama' masnun*, and that is created from dust, as Allah says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersed﴾ [al-Rum: 20].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, 'Awf related to us, Qassamah ibn Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah created Adam from a handful He took from all of the earth, so the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them is the red, the black, and the white, and what is between those; and the evil and the good, and what is between those."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, through several chains, from 'Awf al-A'rabi, similar to it. [Al-Musnad (4/400), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4693), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2955).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

﴿Then We made him a drop of semen﴾: This pronoun refers to the species of man, as He says in another verse: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his offspring from an extract of worthless fluid﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7-8], meaning weak, as He says: ﴿Did We not create you from a worthless fluid? And We placed it in a secure place﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20-21], meaning the womb, prepared and readied for that, ﴿for a known period﴾ [al-Mursalat: 22], and a known term, and a specified time, until it became firm and passed from one state to another and from one attribute to another. For this reason He says here: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾, meaning: then We transformed the drop, which is the gushing fluid that issues from the loins of the man, which is his back, and the breastbones of the woman, which are the bones of her chest between the collarbone and the nipple, so it became a red clinging clot, shaped like a leech, elongated. 'Ikrimah said: it is blood.

﴿Then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾: It is a piece like a morsel of flesh, having no form and no outline. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, meaning: We shaped it with a head, two hands, and two feet, with its bones, its sinews, and its veins.

Others recited: ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾ [in some readings: "the drop bones"]. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the bone of the spine.

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every part of the son of Adam decays except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reassembled."

﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, meaning: and We placed upon that what covers it, binds it, and strengthens it. ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: then We breathed the spirit into it, and it moved, and became ﴿another creation﴾, possessing hearing, sight, perception, movement, and motion. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Ja'far ibn Musafir related to us, Yahya ibn Hassan related to us, al-Nadr (meaning Ibn Kathir, client of the Banu Hashim) related to us, Zayd ibn 'Ali related to us, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the drop completes four months, an angel is sent to it, and he breathes the spirit into it in the three darknesses. That is His saying: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: We breathed the spirit into it.

It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the breathing of the spirit.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning by it: the spirit. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/81).]

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾, meaning: We move him from state to state, until he emerges as an infant, then grows up as a child, then reaches puberty, then becomes a youth, then a middle-aged man, then an old man, then decrepit.

Similar to this is narrated from Qatadah and al-Dahhak. There is no contradiction, for from the beginning of the breathing of the spirit into him, he began these transitions and states. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abd Allah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to us, and he is the truthful and the believed: "Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for the same period, then he becomes a lump for the same period. Then the angel is sent to him, and he breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or fortunate. By He other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Book precedes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed a man may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit, then the Book precedes him, and he is sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash. [Al-Musnad (1/382), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6594), Sahih Muslim no. (2643).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah related to us from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, who said: 'Abd Allah (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) said: When the drop falls into the womb, it spreads into every hair and nail, then it remains for forty days, then it slides down in the womb and becomes a clot.

Imam Ahmad also said: Husayn ibn al-Hasan related to us, Abu Kudaynah related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from 'Abd Allah, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was narrating to his companions. Quraysh said: "O Jew, this man claims that he is a prophet." He said: "I will surely ask him about something that none but a prophet knows." So he came and sat down and said: "O Muhammad, from what is man created?" He said: "O Jew, from both: from the drop of the man and from the drop of the woman. As for the drop of the man, it is a thick drop from which come the bone and the sinew; and as for the drop of the woman, it is a thin drop from which come the flesh and the blood." The Jew stood up and said: "Thus used to say those before you." [Al-Musnad (1/465).]

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us from 'Amr, from Abu al-Tufayl, Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The angel enters upon the drop after it settles in the womb by forty nights, and says: 'O Lord, what? Is he wretched or fortunate? Is he male or female?' Allah decrees, and the two write. They say: 'What? Male or female?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees, and the two write, and his deeds, his traces, his calamity, and his provision are written. Then the scroll is folded, and nothing is added to what is in it nor subtracted from it."

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, that is Ibn Dinar, with the same meaning. And from other chains, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd Abu Surayhah al-Ghifari, similar to it. And Allah knows best. [Sahih Muslim no. (2644), and no. (2645).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has appointed over the womb an angel who says: 'O Lord, a drop. O Lord, a clot. O Lord, a lump.' When Allah wills to create it, he says: 'O Lord, male or female? Wretched or fortunate? What is the provision and the term?'" He said: "So that is written in the belly of its mother."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (318), Sahih Muslim no. (2646).]

* *

His saying: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, meaning: when He mentioned His power and His subtle care in creating this drop from state to state and from form to form, until it took shape and became the complete, perfectly formed human being, He said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib related to us, Abu Dawud related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd related to us, from Anas, who said: 'Umar, meaning Ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I agreed with my Lord in four things: this verse was revealed: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ to the end of the verse, and I said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. Then it was revealed: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾."

He also said: My father related to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us, Shaybān related to us, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah dictated to me this verse: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ up to His saying: ﴿another creation﴾. Then Mu'adh said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed. Mu'adh said to him: "At what did you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "With it the verse was concluded: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (3367), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," from Abu Zur'ah, from Adam ibn Iyas with it; Jabir al-Ju'fi is weak.]

Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi is extremely weak, and in this report there is severe strangeness, because this sura is Meccan, Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote down the revelation in Medina, and similarly the conversion of Mu'adh ibn Jabal also took place in Medina. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then indeed you, after that, are surely dead﴾, meaning: after this first origination from non-existence, you will come to death. ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected﴾, meaning: the final origination. ﴿Then Allah originates the final creation﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 20], meaning: on the Day of Return, and the rising of the spirits and the bodies, when He will call the creation to account and repay every worker for his deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 23, verse 17:

When Allah the Exalted mentioned the creation of man, He followed it with mention of the creation of the seven heavens. Allah often mentions the creation of the heavens and the earth together with the creation of man, as He said: ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57]. Likewise at the beginning of Surat as-Sajdah (Alif Lam Mim), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite on the morning of Friday, its opening is the creation of the heavens and the earth, then the explanation of the creation of man from an extract of clay, and in it is the matter of the Return and the Recompense, and other purposes.

As for His words ﴿seven paths﴾: Mujahid said: it means the seven heavens. This is like His saying: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them exalt Him﴾ [al-Isra: 44], ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ [Nuh: 15], ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends among them that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [at-Talaq: 12]. And thus He said here: ﴿And We have created above you seven paths, and We are not unaware of the creation﴾. That is: He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it, and He is with you wherever you are, and Allah is Seeing of what you do. He, glory be to Him, is not screened from Him one heaven from another heaven, nor one earth from another earth, nor one mountain, except that He knows what is in its crevice; and no sea except that He knows what is in its depth. He knows the number of what is in the mountains, the hills, the sands, the seas, the deserts and the trees, ﴿And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

يذكر الله تعالى نعمه على عباده التي لا تُعَدّ ولا تُحصى، في إنزاله المطر من السماء ﴿بِقَدَرٍ﴾، أي: بحسب الحاجة، لا كثيرًا فيُفسد الأرض والعمران، ولا قليلًا فلا يكفي الزروع والثمار، بل بقدر الحاجة إليه من السقي والشرب والانتفاع به، حتى إن الأراضي التي تحتاج ماءً كثيرًا لزرعها ولا تحتمل دِمنتُها إنزالَ المطر عليها، يسوق إليها الماءَ من بلاد أخرى، كما في أرض مصر، ويقال لها: "الأرض الجُرُز"، يسوق الله إليها ماء النيل معه طينٌ أحمر يجترفه من بلاد الحبشة في زمان أمطارها، فيأتي الماءُ يحمل طينًا أحمر، فيسقي أرضَ مصر، ويقرّ الطينُ على أرضهم ليزدرعوا فيه، لأن أرضهم سِباخٌ يغلب عليها الرمال، فسبحان اللطيف الخبير الرحيم الغفور.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الأرْضِ﴾ أي: جعلنا الماءَ إذا نزل من السحاب يَخلُد في الأرض، وجعلنا في الأرض قابليّةً له، تشربه ويتغذى به ما فيها من الحَبّ والنوى.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَى ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ﴾ أي: لو شئنا ألّا تُمطِر لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لصرفناه عنكم إلى السِّباخ والبراري [والبحار] [زيادة من ف وأ] والقفار لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه أُجاجًا لا يُنتفع به لشرب ولا لسقي لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه لا ينزل في الأرض، بل ينجرّ على وجهها لفعلنا. ولو شئنا لجعلناه إذا نزل فيها يغور إلى مدى لا تصلون إليه ولا تنتفعون به لفعلنا. ولكن بلطفه ورحمته يُنزِل عليكم الماءَ من السحاب عذبًا فُراتًا زُلالًا، فيُسكنه في الأرض ويسلكه ينابيعَ في الأرض، فيَفتح العيونَ والأنهار، فيَسقي به الزروعَ والثمار، وتشربون منه ودوابّكم وأنعامكم، وتغتسلون منه وتتطهرون وتتنظفون، فله الحمد والمنّة.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَنْشَأْنَا لَكُمْ بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ يعني: فأخرجنا لكم بما أنزلنا من الماء ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾، أي: بساتين وحدائق ذاتَ بهجة، أي: ذاتَ منظر حسن.

* *

وقوله: ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ أي: فيها نخيل وأعناب. وهذا ما كان يألف أهلُ الحجاز، ولا فرقَ بين الشيء وبين نظيره، وكذلك في حق كل أهل إقليم، عندهم من الثمار من نعمة الله عليهم ما يعجزون عن القيام بشكره.

* *

وقوله: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَوَاكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ﴾ أي: من جميع الثمار، كما قال: ﴿يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالأعْنَابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ [النحل: 11].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ كأنه معطوف على شيء مقدَّر، تقديرُه: تنظرون إلى حسنه ونضجه، ومنه تأكلون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ﴾ يعني: الزيتونةَ. والطُّور: هو الجبل. وقال بعضهم: إنما يُسمّى طورًا إذا كان فيه شجرٌ، فإن عَرِيَ عنها سُمّي جبلًا لا طورًا، والله أعلم. وطور سيناء: هو طور سينين، وهو الجبل الذي كلّم [الله] [زيادة من ف، وفي أ: "والله تعالى"] عليه موسى بن عمران، عليه السلام، وما حوله من الجبال التي فيها شجرُ الزيتون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾: قال بعضهم: الباء زائدة، وتقديره: تُنبت الدُّهنَ، كما في قول العرب: "أَلْقى فلانٌ بيدِه"، أي: يدَه. وأما على قول من يُضمّن الفعلَ فتقديرُه: تخرج بالدهن، أو [في ف، أ: "أي"] تأتي بالدهن؛ ولهذا قال: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ﴾، أي: إدام، قاله قتادة. ﴿لِلآكِلِينَ﴾ أي: فيها ما ينتفع به من الدهن والاصطباغ، كما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا وكيع، عن عبد الله بن عيسى، عن عطاء الشامي، عن أبي أُسَيد -واسمه مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي الأنصاري- قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "كلوا الزيتَ وادَّهِنوا به؛ فإنه من شجرة مباركة" [المسند (3/497)].

وقال عبد بن حميد في مسنده وتفسيره: حدثنا عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا معمر، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، عن عمر؛ أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: "ائتدموا بالزيت وادَّهنوا به، فإنه يخرج من شجرة مباركة".

ورواه الترمذي وابن ماجه من غير وجه، عن عبد الرزاق [المنتخب لعبد بن حميد برقم (13)، وسنن الترمذي برقم (1851)، وسنن ابن ماجه برقم (3319)]. قال الترمذي: ولا يُعرف إلا من حديثه، وكان يضطرب فيه، فربما ذكر فيه عُمر [في أ: "عمرو"] وربما لم يذكره.

قال أبو القاسم الطبراني: حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل، حدثنا أبي، حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة، حدثني الصعب بن حكيم بن شريك بن نملة، عن أبيه عن جده، قال: ضِفتُ عمرَ بن الخطاب ليلةَ عاشوراء [في ف: "ضفت ليلة عمر بن الخطاب"]، فأطعمني [في ف: "عودًا". وفي أ: "عسورًا"] من رأس بعير بارد، وأطعمنا زيتًا، وقال: هذا الزيتُ المباركُ الذي قال اللهُ لنبيِّه ﷺ [المعجم الكبير (1/74)، والصعب بن حكيم لا يُعرف كما قال الذهبي].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ﴾: يذكر تعالى ما جعل لخلقه في الأنعام من المنافع، وذلك أنهم يشربون من ألبانها الخارجةِ من بين فَرْثٍ ودمٍ، ويأكلون من حُملانها، ويلبسون من أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها، ويركبون ظهورَها ويُحمِّلونها [في ف: "ويحملون"] الأحمالَ الثقالَ إلى البلاد النائية عنهم، كما قال تعالى: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَالِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ الأنْفُسِ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [النحل: 7]، وقال تعالى: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَا أَنْعَامًا فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ. وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ. وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [يس: 71-73].

يذكر الله تعالى نعمه على عباده التي لا تُعَدّ ولا تُحصى، في إنزاله المطر من السماء ﴿بِقَدَرٍ﴾، أي: بحسب الحاجة، لا كثيرًا فيُفسد الأرض والعمران، ولا قليلًا فلا يكفي الزروع والثمار، بل بقدر الحاجة إليه من السقي والشرب والانتفاع به، حتى إن الأراضي التي تحتاج ماءً كثيرًا لزرعها ولا تحتمل دِمنتُها إنزالَ المطر عليها، يسوق إليها الماءَ من بلاد أخرى، كما في أرض مصر، ويقال لها: "الأرض الجُرُز"، يسوق الله إليها ماء النيل معه طينٌ أحمر يجترفه من بلاد الحبشة في زمان أمطارها، فيأتي الماءُ يحمل طينًا أحمر، فيسقي أرضَ مصر، ويقرّ الطينُ على أرضهم ليزدرعوا فيه، لأن أرضهم سِباخٌ يغلب عليها الرمال، فسبحان اللطيف الخبير الرحيم الغفور.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الأرْضِ﴾ أي: جعلنا الماءَ إذا نزل من السحاب يَخلُد في الأرض، وجعلنا في الأرض قابليّةً له، تشربه ويتغذى به ما فيها من الحَبّ والنوى.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَى ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ﴾ أي: لو شئنا ألّا تُمطِر لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لصرفناه عنكم إلى السِّباخ والبراري [والبحار] [زيادة من ف وأ] والقفار لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه أُجاجًا لا يُنتفع به لشرب ولا لسقي لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه لا ينزل في الأرض، بل ينجرّ على وجهها لفعلنا. ولو شئنا لجعلناه إذا نزل فيها يغور إلى مدى لا تصلون إليه ولا تنتفعون به لفعلنا. ولكن بلطفه ورحمته يُنزِل عليكم الماءَ من السحاب عذبًا فُراتًا زُلالًا، فيُسكنه في الأرض ويسلكه ينابيعَ في الأرض، فيَفتح العيونَ والأنهار، فيَسقي به الزروعَ والثمار، وتشربون منه ودوابّكم وأنعامكم، وتغتسلون منه وتتطهرون وتتنظفون، فله الحمد والمنّة.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَنْشَأْنَا لَكُمْ بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ يعني: فأخرجنا لكم بما أنزلنا من الماء ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾، أي: بساتين وحدائق ذاتَ بهجة، أي: ذاتَ منظر حسن.

* *

وقوله: ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ أي: فيها نخيل وأعناب. وهذا ما كان يألف أهلُ الحجاز، ولا فرقَ بين الشيء وبين نظيره، وكذلك في حق كل أهل إقليم، عندهم من الثمار من نعمة الله عليهم ما يعجزون عن القيام بشكره.

* *

وقوله: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَوَاكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ﴾ أي: من جميع الثمار، كما قال: ﴿يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالأعْنَابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ [النحل: 11].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ كأنه معطوف على شيء مقدَّر، تقديرُه: تنظرون إلى حسنه ونضجه، ومنه تأكلون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ﴾ يعني: الزيتونةَ. والطُّور: هو الجبل. وقال بعضهم: إنما يُسمّى طورًا إذا كان فيه شجرٌ، فإن عَرِيَ عنها سُمّي جبلًا لا طورًا، والله أعلم. وطور سيناء: هو طور سينين، وهو الجبل الذي كلّم [الله] [زيادة من ف، وفي أ: "والله تعالى"] عليه موسى بن عمران، عليه السلام، وما حوله من الجبال التي فيها شجرُ الزيتون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾: قال بعضهم: الباء زائدة، وتقديره: تُنبت الدُّهنَ، كما في قول العرب: "أَلْقى فلانٌ بيدِه"، أي: يدَه. وأما على قول من يُضمّن الفعلَ فتقديرُه: تخرج بالدهن، أو [في ف، أ: "أي"] تأتي بالدهن؛ ولهذا قال: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ﴾، أي: إدام، قاله قتادة. ﴿لِلآكِلِينَ﴾ أي: فيها ما ينتفع به من الدهن والاصطباغ، كما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا وكيع، عن عبد الله بن عيسى، عن عطاء الشامي، عن أبي أُسَيد -واسمه مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي الأنصاري- قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "كلوا الزيتَ وادَّهِنوا به؛ فإنه من شجرة مباركة" [المسند (3/497)].

وقال عبد بن حميد في مسنده وتفسيره: حدثنا عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا معمر، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، عن عمر؛ أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: "ائتدموا بالزيت وادَّهنوا به، فإنه يخرج من شجرة مباركة".

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ﴾: يذكر تعالى ما جعل لخلقه في الأنعام من المنافع، وذلك أنهم يشربون من ألبانها الخارجةِ من بين فَرْثٍ ودمٍ، ويأكلون من حُملانها، ويلبسون من أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها، ويركبون ظهورَها ويُحمِّلونها [في ف: "ويحملون"] الأحمالَ الثقالَ إلى البلاد النائية عنهم، كما قال تعالى: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَالِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ الأنْفُسِ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [النحل: 7]، وقال تعالى: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَا أَنْعَامًا فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ. وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ. وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [يس: 71-73].

يذكر الله تعالى نعمه على عباده التي لا تُعَدّ ولا تُحصى، في إنزاله المطر من السماء ﴿بِقَدَرٍ﴾، أي: بحسب الحاجة، لا كثيرًا فيُفسد الأرض والعمران، ولا قليلًا فلا يكفي الزروع والثمار، بل بقدر الحاجة إليه من السقي والشرب والانتفاع به، حتى إن الأراضي التي تحتاج ماءً كثيرًا لزرعها ولا تحتمل دِمنتُها إنزالَ المطر عليها، يسوق إليها الماءَ من بلاد أخرى، كما في أرض مصر، ويقال لها: "الأرض الجُرُز"، يسوق الله إليها ماء النيل معه طينٌ أحمر يجترفه من بلاد الحبشة في زمان أمطارها، فيأتي الماءُ يحمل طينًا أحمر، فيسقي أرضَ مصر، ويقرّ الطينُ على أرضهم ليزدرعوا فيه، لأن أرضهم سِباخٌ يغلب عليها الرمال، فسبحان اللطيف الخبير الرحيم الغفور.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الأرْضِ﴾ أي: جعلنا الماءَ إذا نزل من السحاب يَخلُد في الأرض، وجعلنا في الأرض قابليّةً له، تشربه ويتغذى به ما فيها من الحَبّ والنوى.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَى ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ﴾ أي: لو شئنا ألّا تُمطِر لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لصرفناه عنكم إلى السِّباخ والبراري [والبحار] [زيادة من ف وأ] والقفار لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه أُجاجًا لا يُنتفع به لشرب ولا لسقي لفعلنا، ولو شئنا لجعلناه لا ينزل في الأرض، بل ينجرّ على وجهها لفعلنا. ولو شئنا لجعلناه إذا نزل فيها يغور إلى مدى لا تصلون إليه ولا تنتفعون به لفعلنا. ولكن بلطفه ورحمته يُنزِل عليكم الماءَ من السحاب عذبًا فُراتًا زُلالًا، فيُسكنه في الأرض ويسلكه ينابيعَ في الأرض، فيَفتح العيونَ والأنهار، فيَسقي به الزروعَ والثمار، وتشربون منه ودوابّكم وأنعامكم، وتغتسلون منه وتتطهرون وتتنظفون، فله الحمد والمنّة.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَأَنْشَأْنَا لَكُمْ بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ يعني: فأخرجنا لكم بما أنزلنا من الماء ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾، أي: بساتين وحدائق ذاتَ بهجة، أي: ذاتَ منظر حسن.

* *

وقوله: ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ﴾ أي: فيها نخيل وأعناب. وهذا ما كان يألف أهلُ الحجاز، ولا فرقَ بين الشيء وبين نظيره، وكذلك في حق كل أهل إقليم، عندهم من الثمار من نعمة الله عليهم ما يعجزون عن القيام بشكره.

* *

وقوله: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَوَاكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ﴾ أي: من جميع الثمار، كما قال: ﴿يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالأعْنَابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ﴾ [النحل: 11].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ كأنه معطوف على شيء مقدَّر، تقديرُه: تنظرون إلى حسنه ونضجه، ومنه تأكلون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ﴾ يعني: الزيتونةَ. والطُّور: هو الجبل. وقال بعضهم: إنما يُسمّى طورًا إذا كان فيه شجرٌ، فإن عَرِيَ عنها سُمّي جبلًا لا طورًا، والله أعلم. وطور سيناء: هو طور سينين، وهو الجبل الذي كلّم [الله] [زيادة من ف، وفي أ: "والله تعالى"] عليه موسى بن عمران، عليه السلام، وما حوله من الجبال التي فيها شجرُ الزيتون.

* *

وقوله: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾: قال بعضهم: الباء زائدة، وتقديره: تُنبت الدُّهنَ، كما في قول العرب: "أَلْقى فلانٌ بيدِه"، أي: يدَه. وأما على قول من يُضمّن الفعلَ فتقديرُه: تخرج بالدهن، أو [في ف، أ: "أي"] تأتي بالدهن؛ ولهذا قال: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ﴾، أي: إدام، قاله قتادة. ﴿لِلآكِلِينَ﴾ أي: فيها ما ينتفع به من الدهن والاصطباغ، كما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا وكيع، عن عبد الله بن عيسى، عن عطاء الشامي، عن أبي أُسَيد -واسمه مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي الأنصاري- قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "كلوا الزيتَ وادَّهِنوا به؛ فإنه من شجرة مباركة" [المسند (3/497)].

وقال عبد بن حميد في مسنده وتفسيره: حدثنا عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا معمر، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، عن عمر؛ أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: "ائتدموا بالزيت وادَّهنوا به، فإنه يخرج من شجرة مباركة".

وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ﴾: يذكر تعالى ما جعل لخلقه في الأنعام من المنافع، وذلك أنهم يشربون من ألبانها الخارجةِ من بين فَرْثٍ ودمٍ، ويأكلون من حُملانها، ويلبسون من أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها، ويركبون ظهورَها ويُحمِّلونها [في ف: "ويحملون"] الأحمالَ الثقالَ إلى البلاد النائية عنهم، كما قال تعالى: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَالِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ الأنْفُسِ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [النحل: 7]، وقال تعالى: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَا أَنْعَامًا فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ. وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ. وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [يس: 71-73].

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, exalted is He, informs us about Nuh (peace be upon him) when He sent him to his people, to warn them of Allah's punishment, His severe might, and His vengeance against those who associated others with Him, opposed His command, and denied His messengers. ﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ That is: will you not fear Allah for associating others with Him?

Then the chiefs (al-mala'), who were their leaders and elders, said: ﴿This is not but a man like you who wants to make himself superior over you.﴾ They mean: he wants to elevate himself over you and magnify himself by claiming prophethood, though he is a human being like you. So how could revelation be sent to him rather than to you? ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels.﴾ That is: if He had wanted to send a prophet, He would have sent an angel from Himself, not a human being. ﴿We have not heard of this among our forefathers of old.﴾ That is: of the sending of a human being among our earliest forefathers. They mean by this their ancestors, their grandfathers, and the past nations.

And His saying: ﴿He is only a man possessed by madness﴾ means: he is insane in what he claims, that Allah has sent him to you and singled him out from among you with revelation. ﴿So wait for him for a time﴾ means: await with him the calamities of death, and be patient with him for a period until you are rid of him.

Ibn Kathir said, explaining what Allah the Exalted reports about Nuh (peace be upon him): he called upon his Lord, asking for victory over his people, as Allah the Exalted mentions in another verse: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so give victory."﴾ [al-Qamar: 10]. And here He says: ﴿He said, "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me."﴾ At that point Allah commanded him to build the ship, to make it firm and perfect, and to carry in it two of every kind, that is, a male and a female of every species of animals, plants, fruits, and other things, and to carry in it his family ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, meaning those against whom Allah's decree of destruction had already been issued, namely those of his family who did not believe in him, such as his son and his wife. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾, meaning: at the time of witnessing the sending down of the great rain, do not let compassion for your people or pity for them take hold of you, nor hope that their delay might lead them to believe, for I have already decreed that they will be drowned because of their disbelief and transgression. The story has already been explained in detail in Surah Hud [see verses 25–48], so there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

His saying: ﴿So when you have settled, you and those with you, upon the ship, then say, "Praise be to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."﴾ This is as He said: ﴿And He has made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated on them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that. And indeed, to our Lord we will return."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 12–14]. Nuh (peace be upon him) complied with this, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And he said, "Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage."﴾ [Hud: 41]. So he mentioned Allah at the beginning of its voyage and at its end. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾, meaning: indeed, in this act, namely the saving of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers, ﴿are signs﴾, meaning clear proofs and evidences of the truthfulness of the prophets in what they conveyed from Allah the Exalted, and that He the Exalted does what He wills, is capable of everything, and knows everything.

His saying: ﴿And indeed, We were ever going to test [the servants]﴾, meaning: We were ever going to test the servants by sending the messengers.

Ibn Kathir says: God informs that He brought into being, after the people of Noah, another generation (qarn ākharīn). It has been said: the intended people are ʿAd, for they were made successors after them. It has also been said: the intended people are Thamud, because of His saying: ﴿So the Cry seized them in truth﴾. God sent among them a messenger from among themselves, who called them to worship God alone, without partner. But they denied him and opposed him, and they refused to follow him because he was a human being like them. They disdained to follow a human messenger. They denied the meeting with God on the Day of Resurrection and rejected the bodily return (al-maʿād al-juthmānī). They said: ﴿Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth? Far, far is what you are promised!﴾ That is, that is far, far away.

﴿He is only a man who has fabricated against God a lie.﴾ That is, concerning what he has brought you of the message, the warning, and the report of the return. ﴿And we are not believers in him.﴾ ﴿He said: "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me."﴾ That is, the Messenger sought victory over them and asked his Lord to support him against them, so He answered his supplication. ﴿He said: "In a little while they will surely become regretful."﴾ That is, because of your opposition and obstinacy toward what you brought them.

﴿So the Cry seized them in truth﴾. That is, they deserved this from God because of their disbelief and transgression.

The apparent meaning is that a cry gathered upon them together with a violent, strong, cold wind, ﴿destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 25].

* *

His saying: ﴿So We made them debris (ghuthāʾ)﴾. That is, struck down and dead, like the debris of a torrent, which is the worthless, trifling, perished thing from which nothing benefits. ﴿So away with the wrongdoing people!﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 76]. That is, by their disbelief, obstinacy, and opposition to the Messenger of God. So let those who hear beware of denying their messenger.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 23, verses 42–44:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then We produced after them other generations﴾, that is, nations and creatures, ﴿No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it﴾. That is: rather, they are [[In F and A: "bal" (rather) in place of "yaʿni" (that is).]] : rather, they are brought forth [[In F and A: "yuwjadun" (they come into existence) in place of "yu'khadhun" (they are seized/brought).]] according to what Allah the Exalted has decreed for them in His Preserved Book and knew before their existence: nation after nation, generation after generation, age after age, and successor after predecessor.

﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾. Ibn Abbas said: that is, they follow one another. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut"; so among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed﴾ [An-Nahl: 36]. And His saying: ﴿Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him﴾, meaning: most of them and the majority of them, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them except that they mock him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 30].

* *

His saying: ﴿So We followed some of them with others﴾, that is, We destroyed them, like His saying: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah﴾ [Al-Isra: 17].

﴿And We made them narratives﴾, that is, reports and tales for the people, like His saying: ﴿So We made them tales and scattered them completely﴾ [the verse] [[Added from F. In H: "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe."]] [Saba: 19] [ ﴿So away with the people who do not believe﴾ ] [[Added from F.]].

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verses 45–49:

Allah informs that He sent His messenger Musa (peace be upon him) and his brother Harun to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs, with signs, decisive proofs, and conclusive evidences. Fir'awn and his people were arrogant toward following them both and submitting to their command, because they were mere humans, just as the earlier nations denied the sending of messengers from among mankind. Their hearts were alike, so Allah destroyed Fir'awn and his chiefs and drowned them all together on a single day. And He sent down to Musa the Book, which is the Torah, containing its rulings, commands, and prohibitions. This was after Allah had crushed Fir'awn and the Copts and seized them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Able. And after Allah sent down the Torah, He did not destroy a nation with a general destruction; rather, He commanded the believers to fight the disbelievers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations, as insights for mankind, and guidance and mercy, that they might remember﴾ [al-Qasas: 43].

Ibn Kathir said, may God Most High relate concerning His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both, that He made them both a sign for mankind: that is, a conclusive proof of His power over whatever He wills. For He created Adam without a father or a mother, created Hawwa' (Eve) from a male without a female, created Jesus from a female without a male, and created the rest of mankind from a male and a female.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water﴾, Ad-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: "ar-Rabwah (the high ground) is an elevated place of the earth, and it is the best place for vegetation to grow." Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said likewise.

Ibn 'Abbas said: as for His saying ﴿a place of settlement﴾, it means a place of fertility, and ﴿and flowing water﴾ means apparent (clear) water.

Mujahid said: "a level high ground."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿a place of settlement and flowing water﴾: the water was level (still) in it. Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿flowing water﴾ means running water.

Then the exegetes differed about the location of this high ground, in which land of God it is. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "High grounds exist only in Egypt, and when the water flows, the villages are upon these high grounds; were it not for the high grounds, the villages would be drowned."

Something similar is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, and it is very far-fetched.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib concerning His saying: ﴿We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water﴾, he said: "It is Damascus."

He said: and something similar is related from 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam and Khalid ibn Ma'dan.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a place of settlement and flowing water﴾, he said: "The rivers of Damascus."

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: ﴿We gave them refuge on a high ground [a place of settlement and flowing water]﴾, he said: "Jesus son of Mary and his mother, when they took refuge in the Ghouta of Damascus and its surroundings."

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Bishr ibn Rafi', from Abu 'Abd Allah, the cousin of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say concerning His saying: ﴿to a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water﴾: "It is ar-Ramlah in Palestine."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi related to us, Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad al-Khawwas Abu 'Utbah related to us, al-Shaybani related to us, from Ibn Wa'lah, from Kurayb al-Sahuli, from Murrah al-Bahzi who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say to a man: "You will die at the high ground," and he died at ar-Ramlah. [In it is 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, who has odd (munkar) narrations.] And this is a very strange hadith.

The closest of these opinions is what al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water﴾, he said: "The ma'in is the running water," and it is the river of which God Most High said: ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾ [Maryam: 24].

Likewise Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: ﴿to a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water﴾ is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This, and God knows best, is the most apparent, because it is the one mentioned in the other verse, and the Qur'an explains one part of itself by another. It is the most deserving thing by which the Qur'an is interpreted; then the sound hadiths; then the reports of the Companions and Successors.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 23, verses 51–56:

Allah, exalted is He, commands His servants, the messengers, upon them be prayers and peace all together, to eat of the lawful (ḥalāl) and to perform righteous deeds. This indicates that the lawful is an aid to righteous action. The prophets, upon them be peace, fulfilled this in its most complete form. They combined every kind of good, in speech and action, in guiding and in advising. May Allah reward them on behalf of His servants with good.

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said, regarding His words ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾, "By Allah, they were not commanded to eat of your yellow or your red, nor of your sweet or your sour. Rather, He said: Take from it what is lawful."

Sa'īd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, regarding ﴿Eat of the good things﴾: "That means the lawful."

Abū Isḥāq al-Sabī'ī said, on the authority of Abū Maysara ibn Shuraḥbīl: "'Īsā ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) used to eat from the spinning of his mother."

In the Ṣaḥīḥ (of al-Bukhārī): "There is no prophet who did not tend sheep." They said: "And you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, I used to herd them for the people of Makkah for a few qirāṭ" (ﷺ) [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, no. 2262, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

In the Ṣaḥīḥ: "Dāwūd (David), upon him be peace, used to eat from the earnings of his own hand" [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, no. 2073, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs: "The most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dāwūd, and the most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dāwūd. He would sleep half the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. He would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would not flee when he met (the enemy)" [[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, no. 1131, and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 1159, from the hadith of 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Narrated to us by my father, narrated to us by Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfi', narrated to us by Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam, on the authority of Ḍamrah ibn Ḥabīb, that Umm 'Abd Allāh, the sister of Shaddād ibn Aws, sent to the Prophet ﷺ a cup of milk at the time of his breaking the fast, while he was fasting. That was at the beginning of the day and in the intense heat. He sent her messenger back and asked: "From where did you get the sheep?" She said: "I bought it with my own money." So he drank from it. When the next day came, Umm 'Abd Allāh, the sister of Shaddād, came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I sent you milk for you to drink, from the length of the day and the intensity of the heat, and you sent back the messenger with it?" He said to her: "With this the messengers were commanded: not to eat except what is good, and not to act except what is righteous" [[Al-Ḥākim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/125) through al-Mu'āfā ibn 'Imrān, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam with similar wording, and he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two Shaykhs did not record it." Al-Dhahabī commented: "I say: Ibn Abī Maryam is weak."]].

It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Jāmi' al-Tirmidhī, and Musnad Aḥmad, with the wording being his, from the hadith of Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq, from 'Adī ibn Thābit, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers. He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed I am Knowing of what you do﴾. And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things that We have provided for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 172]." Then he mentioned a man who lengthens the journey, disheveled and dusty, whose food is unlawful, whose drink is unlawful, whose clothing is unlawful, and who is nourished by the unlawful. He raises his hands to the sky: "O Lord, O Lord!" But how could his supplication be answered? [[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 1015; Sunan al-Tirmidhī, no. 2989; and al-Musnad (6/159).]]

Al-Tirmidhī said: "Ḥasan gharīb (good and rare). We do not know it except from the hadith of Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq."

* *

His words ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾ mean: your religion, O company of prophets, is one religion and one creed (millah), and it is the call to worship Allah alone, with no partner. For this reason He said: ﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾. The discussion of this has already passed in surah al-Anbiyā', and that ﴿one community﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

* *

His words ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects (zubur)﴾ mean: the nations to whom the prophets were sent. ﴿Each faction, rejoicing in what they have﴾ means: they rejoice in the misguidance they are in, because they think they are guided. For this reason He said, threatening them and warning them: ﴿So leave them in their confusion﴾, that is, in their error and misguidance, ﴿until a time﴾, that is, until the time of their perdition and destruction. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them time, a little﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 17], and He said: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon know﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 3].

* *

His words ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, * We hasten for them into good things? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ mean: do these deluded people suppose that what We give them of wealth and children is because of their honor with Us and their high standing with Us? No indeed, the matter is not as they claim in their saying: ﴿We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished﴾ [Saba': 35]. They erred in that, and their hope was lost. Rather, We only do this with them as gradual enticement (istidrāj), respite, and prolonging. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, they do not perceive﴾. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you; Allah only intends to punish them through these in this worldly life, and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 178]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse; We will draw them step by step from where they do not know. * And I will give them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾ [al-Qalam: 44–45]. And He said: ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone, * and to whom I gave extensive wealth, * and children present (with him), * and made life easy for him, * then he desires that I should increase him. * No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our signs﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11–16]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Neither your wealth nor your children will bring you near to Us in position, except one who believes and does righteous deeds; for them is the double reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the upper chambers﴾ [Saba': 37]. The verses on this are many.

Qatādah said regarding His words ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, * We hasten for them into good things? Rather, they do not perceive﴾: "By Allah, these people were deceived regarding their wealth and their children. O son of Ādam, do not judge people by their wealth and their children; rather, judge them by faith and righteous action."

Imam Aḥmad said: Narrated to us Muḥammad [ibn 'Ubayd, narrated to us Aban ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, narrated to us 'Abd Allāh] [[Addition from the manuscripts Fa and A, and from the Musnad.]] ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has distributed your characters among you just as He has distributed your provisions. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He gives religion only to the one He loves. So whoever Allah gives religion has indeed loved him. By He in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit (yuslim) until his heart and his tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbor feels safe from his harm." They said: "And what is his harm, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His oppression and his injustice." "And a servant does not earn wealth from what is unlawful and then spend from it, for it will not be blessed for him; nor give charity from it, for it will not be accepted from him; nor leave it behind his back except that it will be his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed the wicked does not erase the wicked." [[Al-Musnad (1/387).]]

His words ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾ mean: your religion, O company of prophets, is one religion and one creed (millah), and it is the call to worship Allah alone, with no partner. For this reason He said: ﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾. The discussion of this has already passed in surah al-Anbiyā', and that ﴿one community﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

* *

His words ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects (zubur)﴾ mean: the nations to whom the prophets were sent. ﴿Each faction, rejoicing in what they have﴾ means: they rejoice in the misguidance they are in, because they think they are guided. For this reason He said, threatening them and warning them: ﴿So leave them in their confusion﴾, that is, in their error and misguidance, ﴿until a time﴾, that is, until the time of their perdition and destruction. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them time, a little﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 17], and He said: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will soon know﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 3].

* *

His words ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, * We hasten for them into good things? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ mean: do these deluded people suppose that what We give them of wealth and children is because of their honor with Us and their high standing with Us? No indeed, the matter is not as they claim in their saying: ﴿We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished﴾ [Saba': 35]. They erred in that, and their hope was lost. Rather, We only do this with them as gradual enticement (istidrāj), respite, and prolonging. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, they do not perceive﴾. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you; Allah only intends to punish them through these in this worldly life, and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 178]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse; We will draw them step by step from where they do not know. * And I will give them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾ [al-Qalam: 44–45]. And He said: ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone, * and to whom I gave extensive wealth, * and children present (with him), * and made life easy for him, * then he desires that I should increase him. * No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our signs﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11–16]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Neither your wealth nor your children will bring you near to Us in position, except one who believes and does righteous deeds; for them is the double reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the upper chambers﴾ [Saba': 37]. The verses on this are many.

Qatādah said regarding His words ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, * We hasten for them into good things? Rather, they do not perceive﴾: "By Allah, these people were deceived regarding their wealth and their children. O son of Ādam, do not judge people by their wealth and their children; rather, judge them by faith and righteous action."

Imam Aḥmad said: Narrated to us Muḥammad [ibn 'Ubayd, narrated to us Aban ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, narrated to us 'Abd Allāh] [[Addition from the manuscripts Fa and A, and from the Musnad.]] ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has distributed your characters among you just as He has distributed your provisions. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He gives religion only to the one He loves. So whoever Allah gives religion has indeed loved him. By He in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit (yuslim) until his heart and his tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbor feels safe from his harm." They said: "And what is his harm, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His oppression and his injustice." "And a servant does not earn wealth from what is unlawful and then spend from it, for it will not be blessed for him; nor give charity from it, for it will not be accepted from him; nor leave it behind his back except that it will be his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed the wicked does not erase the wicked." [[Al-Musnad (1/387).]]

* *

On the Day of Resurrection He will call them to account for their deeds, which He recorded for them in a written book (kitāb masṭūr) from which nothing is lost. And He said: ﴿How many generations We destroyed before them, and they called out, but it was no time for escape﴾ [Sad: 3].

And His saying: ﴿Do not cry out today; indeed, you will not be helped by Us﴾: meaning, We will not protect you from what has befallen you, whether you cry out or remain silent. There is no escape, no refuge, and no shelter; the matter is settled and the punishment is due.

Then He mentioned their greatest sins, saying: ﴿My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, meaning when you were called you refused, and when you were summoned you held back. ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great﴾ [Ghafir: 12].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Arrogant about it, conversing at night, speaking nonsense﴾: there are two opinions regarding its interpretation.

One of them is that "arrogant" describes them at the time of their turning away from the truth and their refusal of it, being arrogant toward it and belittling it and its people. According to this view, the pronoun in ﴿about it﴾ has three possible referents:

The first: it refers to the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) at Makkah. They were blamed because they used to converse at night (yasmurūn) with useless talk (al-hujr).

The second: it refers to the Qur'an. They used to converse at night and speak of the Qur'an with useless talk: "It is magic," "It is poetry," "It is soothsaying," and other false statements.

The third: it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). They would mention him in their night conversations with corrupt statements and would coin false comparisons for him, such as that he was a poet, a soothsayer, a sorcerer, a liar, or a madman. All of this is false. Rather, he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, whom Allah made victorious over them, and He expelled them from the Sacred Precinct in humiliation and disgrace.

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿arrogant about it﴾ is: about the House (the Ka'bah), they boast of it and believe that they are its protectors (awliyā'uh), and they are not, as al-Nasa'i said in the Tafsir section of his Sunan:

We were informed by Ahmad ibn Sulayman, who was informed by 'Ubayd Allah, from Isra'il, from 'Abd al-A'la, that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Night conversation (al-samar) was only disliked when this verse was revealed: ﴿Arrogant about it, conversing at night, speaking nonsense﴾. He said: arrogant about the House, saying: "We are its people." ﴿Conversing at night﴾: he said: they act arrogantly and converse at night in it, and they do not maintain it, and they neglect it.

Ibn Abi Hatim has elaborated here at length, and its essence is this.

Allah says, rebuking the polytheists for their failure to understand the Great Qur'an, to reflect upon it, and for their turning away from it. Yet they have been singled out with this Book, which Allah has not sent down upon any messenger more perfect or more noble than it. This is especially so since their forefathers who died in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), to whom no Book had come and to whom no warner had come, did not have this opportunity. Thus it was fitting for these people to meet the blessing which Allah has bestowed upon them by accepting it, by being grateful for it, by understanding it, and by acting in accordance with its requirements in the hours of the night and at the ends of the day, just as the noble ones among them did, those who embraced Islam and followed the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and may Allah be pleased with them.

Qatadah said: "﴿Do they not reflect upon the Word?﴾ By Allah, if the people had reflected upon it and understood it, they would have found in the Qur'an a restraint from disobeying Allah. But they seized upon that which is ambiguous, and so they perished at that point."

Then He said, rebuking the disbelievers among the Quraysh: ﴿Or have they not recognised their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ That is: do they not know Muhammad, his truthfulness, his trustworthiness and his purity, with which he grew up among them? Could they deny that and be obstinate about it? For this reason Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia: "O King, Allah sent to us a Messenger whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness we know." Likewise, al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said to the deputy of Kisra when they confronted them; and Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb likewise said to the king of the Romans, Heraclius, when he asked him and his companions about the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ, his lineage, his truthfulness and his trustworthiness. They were then still disbelievers who had not embraced Islam, yet despite this they could not do otherwise than speak the truth, so they acknowledged that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"?﴾ relates the saying of the polytheists about the Prophet ﷺ, that he had fabricated the Qur'an, that is, he invented it himself, or that he had madness and did not know what he was saying. He informed us that their hearts do not believe in it, while they know the falsehood of what they say about the Qur'an, for there has come to them from the speech of Allah that which cannot be resisted or repelled. He challenged them and all the people of the earth to bring something like it, but they were unable to do so and will never be able to do so, forever and ever. For this reason He said: ﴿Nay, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ It is possible that this is a circumstantial clause, meaning: while most of them are averse to the truth; and it is possible that it is an informative, independent statement. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah said: "It was reported to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam.' The man said, 'You are calling me to a matter I dislike.' The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, 'Even if you dislike it.' It was also reported to us that he met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam,' and that man became angry and it weighed heavily upon him. The Prophet of Allah said to him, 'Tell me: if you were on a rough, rugged path, and you met a man whose face you recognised and whose lineage you knew, and he called you to a wide, easy path, would you follow him?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are on a path rougher than that one if you were upon it, and I am calling you to something easier than that, if only you were called to it.'" It was also reported to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam,' and that man became angry, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Tell me: of your two young men, one of whom, when he speaks to you, tells the truth, and when you entrust him with something he returns it to you, and the other, when he speaks to you, lies to you, and when you entrust him he betrays you — which of them do you love more?" He said, "Rather, my young man who, when he speaks to me, tells me the truth, and when I entrust him he returns it to me." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Thus are you in the sight of your Lord."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is therein would have been corrupted.﴾ Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: "The truth" is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the meaning is: if Allah had responded to what is in their souls of desires and had ordained affairs in accordance with that, ﴿the heavens and the earth and whoever is therein would have been corrupted.﴾ That is, because of the corruption and diversity of their desires, as He informed of them in their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?﴾ Then He said: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 31-32]. He also said: ﴿Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending, and man is ever niggardly.﴾ [Al-Isra: 100]. And He said: ﴿Or have they a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give people even a speck.﴾ [An-Nisa: 53]. In all of this is a demonstration of the helplessness of the servants and the diversity of their opinions and desires, and that He, exalted is He, is perfect in all His attributes, sayings, actions, legislation, decree, and management of His creation, exalted and sanctified is He; there is no god other than Him, and no lord besides Him.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, We have brought them their reminder,﴾ meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿but they turn away from their reminder.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ Al-Hasan said: "Wages." Qatadah said: "A reward." ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better.﴾ That is: you do not ask them for a fee, nor a reward, nor anything for your calling them to guidance; rather, in that you seek from Allah His abundant reward, as He said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for yourselves. My reward is only from Allah.﴾ [Saba: 47]. And He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, and I am not of those who pretend.﴾ [Sad: 86]. And He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers. Follow those who ask you no reward, and they are guided."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 20-21].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, you call them to a straight path. And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.﴾ Imam Ahmad said:

Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas: that an angel came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — as he saw in sleep — two angels came to him; one sat at his feet and the other at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: "Strike a parable for this man and his community." He said: "His parable and the parable of his community is like a group of travellers who reached the edge of a desert, and they had no provisions with which to cross the desert nor with which to return. While they were in that state, a man came to them wearing a striped green garment, and said: 'Do you see, if I bring you to lush pastures and sweet waters, will you follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then go,' and he brought them to lush pastures and sweet waters, and they ate, drank and grew fat. He said to them: 'Did I not find you in that state, and you promised me that if I brought you to lush pastures and sweet waters you would follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, before you are pastures greener than these, and waters more abundant than these, so follow me.' Then one group said: 'By Allah, he has spoken the truth; let us follow him.' And another group said: 'We are content with this; we will remain upon it.'" [Al-Musnad (1/267)].

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), said: Zuhayr narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated to us, Hafs ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I am holding you back by your waist-wraps, saying: 'Come back from the Fire, come back from the Fire!' But you overpower me and rush into it like moths and locusts. So I am about to release your waist-wraps, and I am your forerunner at the Pool. You will come to me together and in scattered groups; I will recognise you by your marks and your names, as a man recognises a strange camel among his camels. You will be driven to the right and to the left, and I will plead to the Lord of the Worlds concerning you: O Lord, my people, O Lord, my community.

It will be said: 'O Muhammad, you do not know what they innovated after you; they used to walk backward on their heels after you. I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather water-skin, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message.'" [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad (no. 900) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in at-Tamhid (2/300) narrated it by way of Malik ibn Isma'il from Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari with similar wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/85): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and al-Bazzar, except that he said: 'carrying a cushaa (skin-bag) instead of a water-skin.' And the men of all of them are trustworthy."]

Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a hadith with a good chain, except that Hafs ibn Humayd is unknown; I know of no one who narrated from him except Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi."

I say: Rather, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq also narrated from him, and Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "Salih." An-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban declared him reliable.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾ means: they are inclining, deviating, tyrannical, turning aside. The Arabs say: "So-and-so swerved from the road" when he strayed from it.

* *

While they were in that state, a man came to them wearing a striped green garment, and said: 'Do you see, if I bring you to lush pastures and sweet waters, will you follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then go,' and he brought them to lush pastures and sweet waters, and they ate, drank and grew fat. He said to them: 'Did I not find you in that state, and you promised me that if I brought you to lush pastures and sweet waters you would follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' You will be driven to the right and to the left, and I will plead to the Lord of the Worlds concerning you: O Lord, my people, O Lord, my community.

And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message.
