Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), said: Zuhayr narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated to us, Hafs ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I am holding you back by your waist-wraps, saying: 'Come back from the Fire, come back from the Fire!' But you overpower me and rush into it like moths and locusts. So I am about to release your waist-wraps, and I am your forerunner at the Pool. You will come to me together and in scattered groups; I will recognise you by your marks and your names, as a man recognises a strange camel among his camels. You will be driven to the right and to the left, and I will plead to the Lord of the Worlds concerning you: O Lord, my people, O Lord, my community.

It will be said: 'O Muhammad, you do not know what they innovated after you; they used to walk backward on their heels after you. I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather water-skin, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message.'" [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad (no. 900) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in at-Tamhid (2/300) narrated it by way of Malik ibn Isma'il from Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari with similar wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/85): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and al-Bazzar, except that he said: 'carrying a cushaa (skin-bag) instead of a water-skin.' And the men of all of them are trustworthy."]

Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a hadith with a good chain, except that Hafs ibn Humayd is unknown; I know of no one who narrated from him except Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi."

I say: Rather, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq also narrated from him, and Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "Salih." An-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban declared him reliable.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾ means: they are inclining, deviating, tyrannical, turning aside. The Arabs say: "So-and-so swerved from the road" when he strayed from it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what harm is upon them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ He, exalted is He, informs of their obstinacy in their disbelief: that even if He were to relieve their ailments and make them understand the Qur'an, they would not submit to it, but would persist in their disbelief, obstinacy and transgression, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 23]. And He said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers!" But there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars. And they say, "There is none but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ [Al-An'am: 27-29]. This is of the category of His knowledge, exalted is He, of what will not happen; had it happened, how it would have happened.

Ad-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas: "Everything in which there is 'law' (lau, 'if'), it is of that which will never happen."

Allah says, rebuking the polytheists for their failure to understand the Great Qur'an, to reflect upon it, and for their turning away from it. Yet they have been singled out with this Book, which Allah has not sent down upon any messenger more perfect or more noble than it. This is especially so since their forefathers who died in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), to whom no Book had come and to whom no warner had come, did not have this opportunity. Thus it was fitting for these people to meet the blessing which Allah has bestowed upon them by accepting it, by being grateful for it, by understanding it, and by acting in accordance with its requirements in the hours of the night and at the ends of the day, just as the noble ones among them did, those who embraced Islam and followed the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and may Allah be pleased with them.

Qatadah said: "﴿Do they not reflect upon the Word?﴾ By Allah, if the people had reflected upon it and understood it, they would have found in the Qur'an a restraint from disobeying Allah. But they seized upon that which is ambiguous, and so they perished at that point."

Then He said, rebuking the disbelievers among the Quraysh: ﴿Or have they not recognised their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ That is: do they not know Muhammad, his truthfulness, his trustworthiness and his purity, with which he grew up among them? Could they deny that and be obstinate about it? For this reason Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia: "O King, Allah sent to us a Messenger whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness we know." Likewise, al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said to the deputy of Kisra when they confronted them; and Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb likewise said to the king of the Romans, Heraclius, when he asked him and his companions about the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ, his lineage, his truthfulness and his trustworthiness. They were then still disbelievers who had not embraced Islam, yet despite this they could not do otherwise than speak the truth, so they acknowledged that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"?﴾ relates the saying of the polytheists about the Prophet ﷺ, that he had fabricated the Qur'an, that is, he invented it himself, or that he had madness and did not know what he was saying. He informed us that their hearts do not believe in it, while they know the falsehood of what they say about the Qur'an, for there has come to them from the speech of Allah that which cannot be resisted or repelled. He challenged them and all the people of the earth to bring something like it, but they were unable to do so and will never be able to do so, forever and ever. For this reason He said: ﴿Nay, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ It is possible that this is a circumstantial clause, meaning: while most of them are averse to the truth; and it is possible that it is an informative, independent statement. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah said: "It was reported to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam.' The man said, 'You are calling me to a matter I dislike.' The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, 'Even if you dislike it.' It was also reported to us that he met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam,' and that man became angry and it weighed heavily upon him. The Prophet of Allah said to him, 'Tell me: if you were on a rough, rugged path, and you met a man whose face you recognised and whose lineage you knew, and he called you to a wide, easy path, would you follow him?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are on a path rougher than that one if you were upon it, and I am calling you to something easier than that, if only you were called to it.'" It was also reported to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ met a man and said to him, 'Embrace Islam,' and that man became angry, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Tell me: of your two young men, one of whom, when he speaks to you, tells the truth, and when you entrust him with something he returns it to you, and the other, when he speaks to you, lies to you, and when you entrust him he betrays you — which of them do you love more?" He said, "Rather, my young man who, when he speaks to me, tells me the truth, and when I entrust him he returns it to me." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Thus are you in the sight of your Lord."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is therein would have been corrupted.﴾ Mujahid, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: "The truth" is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the meaning is: if Allah had responded to what is in their souls of desires and had ordained affairs in accordance with that, ﴿the heavens and the earth and whoever is therein would have been corrupted.﴾ That is, because of the corruption and diversity of their desires, as He informed of them in their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?﴾ Then He said: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 31-32]. He also said: ﴿Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending, and man is ever niggardly.﴾ [Al-Isra: 100]. And He said: ﴿Or have they a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give people even a speck.﴾ [An-Nisa: 53]. In all of this is a demonstration of the helplessness of the servants and the diversity of their opinions and desires, and that He, exalted is He, is perfect in all His attributes, sayings, actions, legislation, decree, and management of His creation, exalted and sanctified is He; there is no god other than Him, and no lord besides Him.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, We have brought them their reminder,﴾ meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿but they turn away from their reminder.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ Al-Hasan said: "Wages." Qatadah said: "A reward." ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better.﴾ That is: you do not ask them for a fee, nor a reward, nor anything for your calling them to guidance; rather, in that you seek from Allah His abundant reward, as He said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is for yourselves. My reward is only from Allah.﴾ [Saba: 47]. And He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, and I am not of those who pretend.﴾ [Sad: 86]. And He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers. Follow those who ask you no reward, and they are guided."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 20-21].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, you call them to a straight path. And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.﴾ Imam Ahmad said:

Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas: that an angel came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — as he saw in sleep — two angels came to him; one sat at his feet and the other at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: "Strike a parable for this man and his community." He said: "His parable and the parable of his community is like a group of travellers who reached the edge of a desert, and they had no provisions with which to cross the desert nor with which to return. While they were in that state, a man came to them wearing a striped green garment, and said: 'Do you see, if I bring you to lush pastures and sweet waters, will you follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then go,' and he brought them to lush pastures and sweet waters, and they ate, drank and grew fat. He said to them: 'Did I not find you in that state, and you promised me that if I brought you to lush pastures and sweet waters you would follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, before you are pastures greener than these, and waters more abundant than these, so follow me.' Then one group said: 'By Allah, he has spoken the truth; let us follow him.' And another group said: 'We are content with this; we will remain upon it.'" [Al-Musnad (1/267)].

But you overpower me and rush into it like moths and locusts. So I am about to release your waist-wraps, and I am your forerunner at the Pool. You will come to me together and in scattered groups; I will recognise you by your marks and your names, as a man recognises a strange camel among his camels. You will be driven to the right and to the left, and I will plead to the Lord of the Worlds concerning you: O Lord, my people, O Lord, my community.

It will be said: 'O Muhammad, you do not know what they innovated after you; they used to walk backward on their heels after you. I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message. And I will surely recognise one of you who comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather water-skin, calling: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! And I will say: I possess nothing for you; I have conveyed the message.'" [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad (no. 900) and Ibn Abd al-Barr in at-Tamhid (2/300) narrated it by way of Malik ibn Isma'il from Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari with similar wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/85): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and al-Bazzar, except that he said: 'carrying a cushaa (skin-bag) instead of a water-skin.' And the men of all of them are trustworthy."]

Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a hadith with a good chain, except that Hafs ibn Humayd is unknown; I know of no one who narrated from him except Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi."

I say: Rather, Ash'ath ibn Ishaq also narrated from him, and Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "Salih." An-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban declared him reliable.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾ means: they are inclining, deviating, tyrannical, turning aside. The Arabs say: "So-and-so swerved from the road" when he strayed from it.

* *

But there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars. And they say, "There is none but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ [Al-An'am: 27-29]. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment﴾, meaning: We tested them with calamities and hardships. ﴿Yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾, meaning: that did not turn them back from the disbelief and opposition they were in; rather they persisted in their misguidance and deviation. ﴿They did not humble themselves﴾ means they did not submit humbly, and ﴿nor did they entreat﴾ means they did not supplicate, as He says: ﴿Why, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not entreat? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them what they had been doing﴾ [al-An'am: 43].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Hamzah al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Yazid, meaning al-Nahwi (the grammarian), from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: Abu Sufyan came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, I implore you by Allah and by the ties of kinship, for we have eaten al-'Ilhiz," meaning the wool and blood. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾.

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11352).]]. The origin of this hadith in the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Quraysh when they refused to accept, saying: "O Allah, help me against them with seven [years of famine] like the seven [years] of Yusuf" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4693), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2798), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Umar ibn Kaysan narrated to us, from [my father] [[In F and A: "narrated to me."]] Wahb ibn Umar ibn Kaysan, who said: Wahb ibn Munabbih was imprisoned, and a man from the sons [of the Persians] said to him: "Shall I recite to you a line of poetry, O Abu Abdullah?" Wahb said: "We are in a part of Allah's punishment, and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾." He said: Wahb then fasted three consecutive days. It was said to him: "What is this fast, O Abu Abdullah?" He said: "Imprisonment befell us, so we increased our worship," meaning: the imprisonment was a new affliction for us, so we added extra worship.

* *

His saying: ﴿Until, when We open for them a door of severe punishment, behold, they will be in despair therein﴾ means: until the command of Allah came to them and the Hour came upon them suddenly, and there seized them from the punishment of Allah what they had not expected. At that point they despaired of every good and gave up all hope of ease, and their hopes and expectations were cut off.

Then He mentions His blessing upon His servants in giving them hearing, sight and hearts, which are the minds and understanding by which they perceive things and take lessons from the signs in the universe that point to the oneness of Allah the Exalted, and that He is the Doer who chooses whatever He wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾ means: how little is your gratitude to Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, as He says: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you strive, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103].

Then He informs about His great power and overpowering dominion in creating the creation and multiplying them in all regions of the earth, with their differing kinds, languages and characteristics. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will gather the first and the last of them for the appointed time of a known day, leaving none of them behind, small or great, male or female, noble or lowly, except that He will restore him as He originated him. Therefore He says: ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death﴾, meaning: He gives life to decayed bones and causes nations to die. ﴿And His is the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning: by His command the night and the day are subjected, each of them pursuing the other swiftly, alternating without ceasing and not separated by any other time, as He says: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overcome the day; each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾ means: do you not have minds that would guide you to the Mighty, the All-Knowing, who has subdued everything, exalted everything, and to whom everything submits?

Then He said, reporting about those who deny the Resurrection, who resembled those deniers before them: ﴿Rather, they said the like of what the former peoples said. They said: "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? We were promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but the fables of the former peoples"﴾. He means they consider the occurrence of that after they have turned to decay to be far-fetched; ﴿We were promised this, we and our fathers before﴾; they mean that restoration is impossible, and that one who reports it only receives it from the books of the former peoples and their fabrications. This denial and rejection on their part is like His saying, reporting about them: ﴿"When we are bones, decayed?" They say: "That would then be a losing return." But it will be only one shout, and at once they will be on the surface [of the earth]﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 11–14]. And He says: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop [of semen], and then he is an open adversary? And he presents to Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–79].

(4693), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2798), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him).]].

Then He said, reporting about those who deny the Resurrection, who resembled those deniers before them: ﴿Rather, they said the like of what the former peoples said. They said: "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? We were promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but the fables of the former peoples"﴾. He means they consider the occurrence of that after they have turned to decay to be far-fetched; ﴿We were promised this, we and our fathers before﴾; they mean that restoration is impossible, and that one who reports it only receives it from the books of the former peoples and their fabrications. This denial and rejection on their part is like His saying, reporting about them: ﴿"When we are bones, decayed?" They say: "That would then be a losing return." But it will be only one shout, and at once they will be on the surface [of the earth]﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 11–14]. And He says: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop [of semen], and then he is an open adversary? And he presents to Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–79].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment﴾, meaning: We tested them with calamities and hardships. ﴿Yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾, meaning: that did not turn them back from the disbelief and opposition they were in; rather they persisted in their misguidance and deviation. ﴿They did not humble themselves﴾ means they did not submit humbly, and ﴿nor did they entreat﴾ means they did not supplicate, as He says: ﴿Why, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not entreat? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them what they had been doing﴾ [al-An'am: 43].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Hamzah al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Yazid, meaning al-Nahwi (the grammarian), from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: Abu Sufyan came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, I implore you by Allah and by the ties of kinship, for we have eaten al-'Ilhiz," meaning the wool and blood. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾.

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11352).]]. The origin of this hadith in the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Quraysh when they refused to accept, saying: "O Allah, help me against them with seven [years of famine] like the seven [years] of Yusuf" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4693), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2798), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Umar ibn Kaysan narrated to us, from [my father] [[In F and A: "narrated to me."]] Wahb ibn Umar ibn Kaysan, who said: Wahb ibn Munabbih was imprisoned, and a man from the sons [of the Persians] said to him: "Shall I recite to you a line of poetry, O Abu Abdullah?" Wahb said: "We are in a part of Allah's punishment, and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they entreat [Him]﴾." He said: Wahb then fasted three consecutive days. It was said to him: "What is this fast, O Abu Abdullah?" He said: "Imprisonment befell us, so we increased our worship," meaning: the imprisonment was a new affliction for us, so we added extra worship.

* *

His saying: ﴿Until, when We open for them a door of severe punishment, behold, they will be in despair therein﴾ means: until the command of Allah came to them and the Hour came upon them suddenly, and there seized them from the punishment of Allah what they had not expected. At that point they despaired of every good and gave up all hope of ease, and their hopes and expectations were cut off.

Then He mentions His blessing upon His servants in giving them hearing, sight and hearts, which are the minds and understanding by which they perceive things and take lessons from the signs in the universe that point to the oneness of Allah the Exalted, and that He is the Doer who chooses whatever He wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾ means: how little is your gratitude to Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, as He says: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you strive, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103].

Then He informs about His great power and overpowering dominion in creating the creation and multiplying them in all regions of the earth, with their differing kinds, languages and characteristics. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will gather the first and the last of them for the appointed time of a known day, leaving none of them behind, small or great, male or female, noble or lowly, except that He will restore him as He originated him. Therefore He says: ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death﴾, meaning: He gives life to decayed bones and causes nations to die. ﴿And His is the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning: by His command the night and the day are subjected, each of them pursuing the other swiftly, alternating without ceasing and not separated by any other time, as He says: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overcome the day; each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾ means: do you not have minds that would guide you to the Mighty, the All-Knowing, who has subdued everything, exalted everything, and to whom everything submits?

So He said: ﴿Say: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?﴾, meaning: who is its owner, the One who created it, and whoever is in it of animals, plants, fruits, and all kinds of creatures? ﴿If you know.﴾ ﴿They will say: To Allah.﴾ meaning: they will acknowledge to you that this belongs to Allah alone, with no partner. So if that is so, ﴿Say: Will you not then remember?﴾ [meaning: will you not remember] that worship is fitting only to the Creator, the Provider, and not to anyone else.

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ meaning: who is the creator of the upper world with what is in it of shining stars and angels submissive to Him in all its regions and directions, and who is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, that is, the one which is the ceiling of the creatures, as came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "The majesty of Allah is greater than that; indeed His Throne is above His heavens like this," and he gestured with his hand like a dome.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4726, from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

And in the other hadith: "The seven heavens and the seven earths, and whatever is in them and between them, compared to the Kursi (Footstool), are nothing but like a ring thrown down in a desert land; and the Kursi with what it contains, compared to the Throne, is like that ring in that desert."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (5/399) through Ibn Wahb from Ibn Zayd from his father from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him); it was previously cited from the narration of Ibn Mardawayh in the commentary on verse 2 of Surat al-Ra'd.]]

For this reason some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: the distance between the two sides of the Throne from one side to the other is a journey of fifty thousand years, [and its height above the seventh earth is a journey of fifty thousand years].

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: it was called "Arsh (Throne)" only because of its elevation.

al-A'mash narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar: the heavens and the earth in the Throne are like a lamp suspended between the sky and the earth.

Mujahid said: the heavens and the earth in the Throne are nothing but like a ring in a desert land.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ala' ibn Salim narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ammar al-Dhuhni, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas who said: "No one can estimate the measure of the Throne." And in another narration: "except Allah, Mighty and Majestic."[[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in Sifat al-Arsh (q 114) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/282) through al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad from Sufyan from Ammar al-Dhuhni with the same chain. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

Some of the early scholars said: the Throne is of red ruby.

For this reason He says here: ﴿and the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, meaning the great one, and He says at the end of the surah: ﴿the Lord of the Noble Throne﴾, meaning the good and splendid one. The Throne combines greatness in its vastness and loftiness, and splendid beauty; for this reason whoever said it is of red ruby said so.

Ibn Mas'ud said: indeed your Lord has neither night nor day; the light of the Throne is from the light of His Face.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will say: To Allah. Say: Will you not then fear Allah?﴾ meaning: if you acknowledge that He is the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne, will you not fear His punishment and beware of His torment for your worshipping others along with Him and your association of partners with Him?

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya al-Qurashi said in his book "al-Tafakkur wal-I'tibar": Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ja'far informed us, Abdullah ibn Dinar informed me, from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often narrated about a woman in the Jahiliyyah who was on the top of a mountain with her son tending sheep. Her son said to her: "O mother, who created you?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created my father?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created me?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the sky?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the earth?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the mountain?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created these sheep?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Indeed I hear that Allah has a great matter," then he threw himself from the mountain and was torn to pieces.

Ibn Umar said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often narrated this hadith to us.

Abdullah ibn Dinar said: Ibn Umar often narrated this hadith to us.

I say: its chain includes Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Madini, father of the Imam Ali ibn al-Madini, and scholars have spoken about him, so Allah knows best.[[Also narrated by Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (4/178) through Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il from Abdullah ibn Ja'far with it, and he said: "Not preserved; no one narrates it from Ibn Dinar except Abdullah ibn Ja'far." Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Madini is weak according to the imams.]]

﴿Say: In whose hand is the dominion of all things?﴾ meaning: in His hand is the sovereignty. ﴿Whom no creature is there but He holds its forelock﴾ [Hud: 56], meaning: He disposes of it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No, by the One in whose hand is my soul," and when he exerted himself in swearing he would say: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." So He, glorified is He, is the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer. ﴿And He protects, and none can protect against Him, if you know.﴾ When the Arabs had a chieftain among them who gave protection to someone, none would violate his protection, and no one lower than him could grant protection against him, lest he usurp his authority. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And He protects, and none can protect against Him﴾, meaning: He is the great Lord, greater than whom there is none, to whom belong creation and command, whose decree cannot be repelled, who cannot be resisted or opposed; what He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. Allah said: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya: 23], meaning: He is not questioned about what He does, due to His greatness, majesty, subjugation, dominance, might, wisdom and justice, while all creatures will be questioned about their deeds, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92–93].

* *

Then Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, We have brought them the truth﴾, which is the declaration that there is no god but Allah, and We have established clear, sound, decisive proofs for it, ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾, meaning: in their worshipping others besides Allah, for they have no proof for it, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿And whoever invokes with Allah another god, for which he has no proof, then his account is only with his Lord; indeed the disbelievers will not succeed﴾. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

He, Exalted is He, affirms His oneness and His independence in creating, disposing and sovereignty, to guide to the fact that He is the One besides whom there is no god, and that worship is fitting only to Him alone, with no partner. So He said: ﴿Say: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?﴾, meaning: who is its owner, the One who created it, and whoever is in it of animals, plants, fruits, and all kinds of creatures? ﴿If you know.﴾ ﴿They will say: To Allah.﴾ meaning: they will acknowledge to you that this belongs to Allah alone, with no partner. ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ meaning: who is the creator of the upper world with what is in it of shining stars and angels submissive to Him in all its regions and directions, and who is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, that is, the one which is the ceiling of the creatures, as came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "The majesty of Allah is greater than that; indeed His Throne is above His heavens like this," and he gestured with his hand like a dome.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4726, from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Mujahid said: the heavens and the earth in the Throne are nothing but like a ring in a desert land.

Allah said: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya: 23], meaning: He is not questioned about what He does, due to His greatness, majesty, subjugation, dominance, might, wisdom and justice, while all creatures will be questioned about their deeds, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92–93].

* *

His saying: ﴿They will say: To Allah﴾, meaning: they will acknowledge that the great Lord who gives protection and against whom none can protect is Allah, Exalted, alone with no partner. ﴿Say: Then how are you deluded?﴾ meaning: how can your minds be led astray in worshipping others along with Him, while you acknowledge and know this?

Then Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, We have brought them the truth﴾, which is the declaration that there is no god but Allah, and We have established clear, sound, decisive proofs for it, ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾, meaning: in their worshipping others besides Allah, for they have no proof for it, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿And whoever invokes with Allah another god, for which he has no proof, then his account is only with his Lord; indeed the disbelievers will not succeed﴾. Polytheists do not do this on the basis of any proof that led them to the falsehood and misguidance they are in; they only do it by following their fathers and their forebears, the bewildered ignorant ones, as they said: ﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

He, Exalted is He, affirms His oneness and His independence in creating, disposing and sovereignty, to guide to the fact that He is the One besides whom there is no god, and that worship is fitting only to Him alone, with no partner. For this reason He told His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to say to the polytheists who worship others alongside Him, who acknowledge His lordship and that He has no partner in it, yet they still associate others with Him in divinity, worshipping others besides Him, while acknowledging that those they worship do not create anything, do not own anything, and have no independent power over anything; rather they believed that those (idols) bring them near to Him in nearness: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. So He said: ﴿Say: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?﴾, meaning: who is its owner, the One who created it, and whoever is in it of animals, plants, fruits, and all kinds of creatures? ﴿If you know.﴾ ﴿They will say: To Allah.﴾ meaning: they will acknowledge to you that this belongs to Allah alone, with no partner. So if that is so, ﴿Say: Will you not then remember?﴾ [meaning: will you not remember] that worship is fitting only to the Creator, the Provider, and not to anyone else.

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ meaning: who is the creator of the upper world with what is in it of shining stars and angels submissive to Him in all its regions and directions, and who is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, that is, the one which is the ceiling of the creatures, as came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "The majesty of Allah is greater than that; indeed His Throne is above His heavens like this," and he gestured with his hand like a dome.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4726, from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

And in the other hadith: "The seven heavens and the seven earths, and whatever is in them and between them, compared to the Kursi (Footstool), are nothing but like a ring thrown down in a desert land; and the Kursi with what it contains, compared to the Throne, is like that ring in that desert."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (5/399) through Ibn Wahb from Ibn Zayd from his father from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him); it was previously cited from the narration of Ibn Mardawayh in the commentary on verse 2 of Surat al-Ra'd.]]

For this reason some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: the distance between the two sides of the Throne from one side to the other is a journey of fifty thousand years, [and its height above the seventh earth is a journey of fifty thousand years].

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: it was called "Arsh (Throne)" only because of its elevation.

al-A'mash narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar: the heavens and the earth in the Throne are like a lamp suspended between the sky and the earth.

Mujahid said: the heavens and the earth in the Throne are nothing but like a ring in a desert land.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ala' ibn Salim narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ammar al-Dhuhni, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas who said: "No one can estimate the measure of the Throne." And in another narration: "except Allah, Mighty and Majestic."[[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in Sifat al-Arsh (q 114) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/282) through al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad from Sufyan from Ammar al-Dhuhni with the same chain. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

Some of the early scholars said: the Throne is of red ruby.

For this reason He says here: ﴿and the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, meaning the great one, and He says at the end of the surah: ﴿the Lord of the Noble Throne﴾, meaning the good and splendid one. The Throne combines greatness in its vastness and loftiness, and splendid beauty; for this reason whoever said it is of red ruby said so.

Ibn Mas'ud said: indeed your Lord has neither night nor day; the light of the Throne is from the light of His Face.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will say: To Allah. Say: Will you not then fear Allah?﴾ meaning: if you acknowledge that He is the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne, will you not fear His punishment and beware of His torment for your worshipping others along with Him and your association of partners with Him?

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya al-Qurashi said in his book "al-Tafakkur wal-I'tibar": Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ja'far informed us, Abdullah ibn Dinar informed me, from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often narrated about a woman in the Jahiliyyah who was on the top of a mountain with her son tending sheep. Her son said to her: "O mother, who created you?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created my father?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created me?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the sky?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the earth?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created the mountain?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Who created these sheep?" She said: "Allah." He said: "Indeed I hear that Allah has a great matter," then he threw himself from the mountain and was torn to pieces.

Ibn Umar said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often narrated this hadith to us.

Abdullah ibn Dinar said: Ibn Umar often narrated this hadith to us.

I say: its chain includes Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Madini, father of the Imam Ali ibn al-Madini, and scholars have spoken about him, so Allah knows best.[[Also narrated by Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (4/178) through Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il from Abdullah ibn Ja'far with it, and he said: "Not preserved; no one narrates it from Ibn Dinar except Abdullah ibn Ja'far." Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Madini is weak according to the imams.]]

Allah, may He be exalted, declares Himself far above having a son or a partner in dominion. He said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor has there been any god with Him; otherwise each god would have gone off with what he created, and some of them would have overcome others.﴾ That is, if a plurality of gods were supposed, each one of them would have independently held what he creates, and existence would not have been ordered. What is witnessed, however, is that existence is orderly and harmonious, and both the higher and lower worlds are linked to one another in the utmost perfection. ﴿You see no discrepancy in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ (67:3). Then each of them would seek to subdue and oppose the other, so some would rise above others.

The theologians (mutakallimun) expressed this meaning through the argument of mutual exclusion (dalil al-tamanu'), which is that if two or more creators were assumed, and one wished to move a body while the other wished it to remain still, then if the will of neither were fulfilled, both would be powerless, and the Necessary Being (al-wajib) cannot be powerless. It is also impossible for both of their wills to be realized together, due to their contradiction. This impossibility arises only from assuming plurality, so that assumption is itself impossible. But if the will of one of them is realized and not the other's, then the one who prevails is the Necessary Being, and the defeated one is possible in existence, because it does not befit the attribute of the Necessary Being to be subdued. For this reason He said: ﴿And some of them would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe.﴾ That is, exalted is He far above what the wrongdoers and transgressors claim in asserting a son or a partner.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: that is, He knows what is hidden from the creatures and what they witness. ﴿So exalted is He above what they associate﴾: that is, He is sanctified, glorified, exalted, mighty and majestic [above what the wrongdoers and deniers say] [[addition from manuscripts F and A.]].

His saying: "And indeed, We are able to show you that which We promise them" (23:95). That is, if We willed, We would show you the punishments, calamities and trials that We bring upon them.

Then He said, guiding him to the beneficial remedy for mixing with people, which is doing good to the one who does evil, so that his heart is won over, and his enmity turns into friendship and his hatred into love. He said: "Repel evil with that which is better" (23:96). This is like what He said in another verse: "Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a close friend. We have already mentioned, at the discussion of seeking refuge, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Shaytan, from his hamz, his nafkh and his nafth" [[See the discussion of seeking refuge in the tafsir of Surah al-Fatihah.]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 23, verse 99–100:

Almighty God informs us about the condition of the one present at death (al-muhtadar 'inda al-mawt), whether he is a disbeliever or one who has been negligent in the matter of God, and about what they say at that moment, and their request to return to the world so that they may amend what they had corrupted during the span of their lives. Therefore He said: ﴿My Lord, send me back! So that I may do righteousness in that which I have left behind.﴾ No! As He said, the Exalted: ﴿And spend of that which We have provided you, before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I could give charity and be among the righteous." But Allah does not delay a soul when its term has come; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10, 11] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a brief term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no decline?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So are there any intercessors for us to intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we might do other than what we used to do?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain."﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers!" Rather, there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ [al-An'am: 27, 28] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers when they see the punishment, saying, "Is there any way to return?"﴾ [al-Shura: 44] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins. So is there any way to get out?" That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when others were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 11, 12] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do." Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would remember could remember therein? And the warner had come to you. So taste [the punishment], for there are no helpers for the wrongdoers.﴾ [Fatir: 37] So He, the Exalted, mentioned that they ask for a return, and they are not answered, at the time of dying, on the Day of Resurrection, at the time of the presentation before the Almighty, and when they are presented before the Fire, while they are in the depths of the torment of the Blazing Fire.

* *

His saying here: ﴿No! Indeed, it is only a word he is saying.﴾ "Kalla" (no, by no means) is a particle of repulsion and rebuke, meaning: We will not respond to what he asks, nor accept it from him.

* *

His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, it is only a word he is saying.﴾ 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Meaning, every wrongdoing one present at death must inevitably say it.

It is possible that this is the reason (ʿillah) for His saying "kalla," i.e., because it is a word: his request to be returned so that he may do righteousness is a statement from him, and a word with no deed accompanying it. Even if he were returned, he would not do righteousness, and he would be lying in this claim of his, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said concerning ﴿until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, so that I may do righteousness in that which I have left behind."﴾ He said: The Almighty (al-Jabbar) says: ﴿No! Indeed, it is only a word he is saying.﴾

'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah, mawla Ghufrah, said: When you hear God say ﴿No!﴾, He is in fact saying: "He has lied."

[[In F: "kadhdhabat" (she has lied).]]

Qatadah said concerning His saying, ﴿until, when death comes to one of them﴾: He said: Al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad used to say: Let each of you imagine himself as having been visited by death, so that he asks his Lord for a reprieve and He grants it to him, and then let him act in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Qatadah also said: By Allah, he does not wish to return to his family or his clan, but he wishes to return and act in obedience to Allah. So look at the wish of the negligent disbeliever and act upon it, and there is no power except with Allah. Similar was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi.

Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Fudayl – meaning Ibn 'Iyad – narrated to us, from Layth, from Talhah ibn Musarrif, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the disbeliever is placed in his grave, he sees his seat in the Fire. He said: He says, "My Lord, send me back! I will repent and do righteousness." He said: It is said to him, "You have been given long life, as you were given long life." He said: His grave is constricted upon him. He said: He is like one who is being stung, sleeping and startled; the creatures and serpents and scorpions of the earth come upon him.

He also said: My father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Salamah ibn Tammam narrated to me, 'Ali ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from 'A'ishah, that she said: Woe to the people of sins among the people of the graves! There enter upon them in their graves black serpents – or: dark ones – a serpent at his head and a serpent at his feet, biting him until they meet in his middle. That is the punishment in the barzakh about which Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.﴾

Abu Salih and others said concerning His saying, ﴿And behind them﴾: it means in front of them.

Mujahid said: The barzakh is the barrier between this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The barzakh is what lies between this world and the Hereafter. They are neither with the people of this world, eating and drinking, nor with the people of the Hereafter, being recompensed for their deeds.

Abu Sakhr said: The barzakh is the graves; they are neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, so they remain until the Day they are resurrected.

As for His saying, ﴿And behind them is a barrier﴾: it is a threat to these wrongdoers at death of the punishment of the barzakh, as He said: ﴿And behind them is Hell﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], and He said: ﴿And behind him is a severe punishment﴾ [Ibrahim: 17].

* *

His saying: ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, meaning: the punishment will continue for them until the Day of Resurrection, as has come in the hadith: "So he will not cease being punished therein" [narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 1071, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "a hasan gharib hadith"], meaning: in the earth.

Ibn Kathir (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*) on Surah 23, verses 101–104:

He, exalted is He, informs that when the Trumpet is blown with the blast of resurrection, and people rise from their graves, ﴿there will be no kinship among them﴾, meaning that kinship will be of no benefit that day. A parent will not show compassion to his child, nor will he turn to him. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend, though they will be made to see them﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10–11], meaning that a close relative will not ask his close relative, though he sees him. Even if that person carried a burden of sins that weighed heavily on his back, and even if he was the dearest of people to him in the world, he will not turn to him or bear for him even the weight of a mosquito's wing. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. For every man that Day, there will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ ['Abasa: 34–37].

Ibn Mas'ud said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last, then a caller will call out: "Whoever has a grievance, let him come and take his right." He said: Then a man will be glad that he has a right over his father, his child or his wife, even if it is small. The proof of this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, the mawla (freed client) of Banu Hashim, narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from al-Miswar, that is Ibn Makhramah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fatimah is a part of me: what troubles her troubles me, and what pains her pains me. Indeed, kinship is cut off on the Day of Resurrection, except for my kinship, my cause (sabab) and my in-law relation (sihr)." [al-Musnad (4/323)]

This hadith has a basis in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from al-Miswar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fatimah is a part of me: what troubles her troubles me, and what harms her harms me." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3714; Sahih Muslim, no. 2449]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Hamzah ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say from this pulpit: "What is wrong with men who say: 'The kinship of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not benefit his people'? Indeed, by Allah, my kinship is connected in this world and the Hereafter. And I, O people, am your forerunner (fargh) when you come..." Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Farwah ibn Abi al-Mighra' narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani narrated to us, from Abu Sinan Dirar ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When the people of Hell are driven toward it, its flame will meet them, then it will scorch them with one blast, and no flesh will remain except that it falls off the heel." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (4/363) and said: "No one narrated it as a marfu' connected report from Abu Sinan from 'Abd Allah except Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani. Ibn 'Uyaynah, Ibn Fudayl and Jarir narrated it from Abu Sinan, but Ibn Fudayl stopped it at Abu Hurayrah."]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Fazzaz narrated to us: al-Khadir ibn 'Ali ibn Yunus al-Qattan narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Abi al-Harith ibn al-Khadir al-Qattan narrated to us: Sa'd ibn Sa'id [in some copies: Sa'd ibn Abi Sa'id] al-Maqburi narrated to us, from his brother, from his father, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning the saying of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces﴾: "It will scorch them with one blast, so their flesh will flow down onto their heels." [Narrated by al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in Sifat al-Nar, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/117), from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they will be grimacing therein﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it means "frowning".

al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, concerning ﴿and they will be grimacing therein﴾, that he said: "Have you not seen the head with the lips drawn back, its teeth exposed and its lips shrivelled?"

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Ali ibn Ishaq informed us: 'Abd Allah, that is Ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us: Sa'id ibn Yazid informed us, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said concerning ﴿and they will be grimacing therein﴾: "The Fire will burn them, so their upper lip will shrink until it reaches the middle of their head, and their lower lip will hang down until it strikes their navel."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain, and said: "Hasan gharib" (good, strange).

Ibn Kathir (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*) on Surah 23, verses 101–104:

He, exalted is He, informs that when the Trumpet is blown with the blast of resurrection, and people rise from their graves, ﴿there will be no kinship among them﴾, meaning that kinship will be of no benefit that day. A parent will not show compassion to his child, nor will he turn to him. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend, though they will be made to see them﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10–11], meaning that a close relative will not ask his close relative, though he sees him. Even if that person carried a burden of sins that weighed heavily on his back, and even if he was the dearest of people to him in the world, he will not turn to him or bear for him even the weight of a mosquito's wing. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. For every man that Day, there will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ ['Abasa: 34–37].

Ibn Mas'ud said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last, then a caller will call out: "Whoever has a grievance, let him come and take his right." He said: Then a man will be glad that he has a right over his father, his child or his wife, even if it is small. The proof of this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, the mawla (freed client) of Banu Hashim, narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from al-Miswar, that is Ibn Makhramah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fatimah is a part of me: what troubles her troubles me, and what pains her pains me. Indeed, kinship is cut off on the Day of Resurrection, except for my kinship, my cause (sabab) and my in-law relation (sihr)." [al-Musnad (4/323)]

This hadith has a basis in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from al-Miswar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fatimah is a part of me: what troubles her troubles me, and what harms her harms me." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3714; Sahih Muslim, no. 2449]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Hamzah ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say from this pulpit: "What is wrong with men who say: 'The kinship of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not benefit his people'? Indeed, by Allah, my kinship is connected in this world and the Hereafter. And I, O people, am your forerunner (fargh) when you come..." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am so-and-so son of so-and-so," [and his brother said: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so"]. Then I will say to them: "As for lineage, I have known it, but you innovated after me and turned back on your heels." [al-Musnad (3/18)]

We have mentioned in the Musnad of the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [Musnad 'Umar ibn al-Khattab by Ibn Kathir (1/389)], through multiple chains from him, may Allah be pleased with him, that when he married Umm Kulthum bint 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: "By Allah, my only reason is that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Every cause and every lineage will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection, except my cause and my lineage.'"

It was narrated by al-Tabarani, al-Bazzar, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb, al-Bayhaqi, and the Hafiz al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah. [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/45); Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2445, Kashf al-Astar; Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (7/64); al-Mukhtarah by al-Maqdisi no. 281] We have also mentioned that he (i.e., 'Umar) gave her a dowry of forty thousand, out of honour and respect, may Allah be pleased with him. The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated in the biography of Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi', husband of Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), through the route of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi: Sulayman ibn 'Umar ibn al-Aqta' narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every lineage and every in-law relation will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection, except my lineage and my in-law relation." [Tarikh Dimashq (19/119, manuscript); it was also narrated by 'Ali ibn Sa'id from Sulayman ibn 'Umar al-Raqqi, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report; and al-Tabarani recorded it in al-Awsat, no. 3963]. It is also narrated in it through the route of 'Ammar ibn Sayf, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, as a marfu' report: "I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that I should not marry into any of my Ummah, and that none of them should marry into me, except that he would be with me in Paradise, and He granted me that." [Tarikh Dimashq (19/119, manuscript); al-Tabarani in al-Awsat no. 3961, Majma' al-Bahrayn, through the route of Yazid ibn al-Kumayt from 'Ammar ibn Sayf. Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (7/85): "its chain is weak (wahin)". There is also a report on this subject from Ibn Abi Awfa, may Allah be pleased with him.] And from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Sayf, from Isma'il, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr.

As for His saying: ﴿Then as for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful﴾, meaning: whoever's good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, even by one, as Ibn 'Abbas said.

﴿Then those are the successful﴾, meaning: those who prevailed, were saved from the Fire, and were admitted to Paradise.

Ibn 'Abbas also said: Those are the ones who achieved what they sought, and were saved from the evil they fled from.

﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾, meaning: whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds, ﴿those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾, meaning: they failed and perished, and returned with a disastrous transaction.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Isma'il ibn Abi al-Harith narrated to us: Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us: Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, Ja'far ibn Zayd and Mansur ibn Zadhan, from Anas ibn Malik, who traced it up (to the Prophet), who said: "Indeed, Allah has an angel appointed over the scale. A son of Adam will be brought and stood between the two pans of the scale. If his scale is heavy, an angel calls out with a voice that the whole creation can hear: 'So-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which he will never be miserable.' And if his scale is light, an angel calls out with a voice that the whole creation can hear: 'So-and-so has been made wretched with a wretchedness after which he will never be happy.'" [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah, as in the takhrij of al-Ihya' (4098), and said: "Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar alone narrated it."]

Its chain is weak, for Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar is abandoned (matruk).

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain, and said: "Hasan gharib" (good, strange).

This is a rebuke from Allah Most High to the people of the Fire, and a reproach to them for the disbelief, sins, prohibitions and grave matters they committed, which brought about their ruin. So He said: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you, and did you not deny them?﴾ Meaning: I had sent Messengers to you, revealed the Books, and removed your doubts, and no proof remained for you to put forward, as He said: ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the Messengers﴾ [an-Nisa': 165], and He said: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15], and He said: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will say, "Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'" And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." So they will acknowledge their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ [al-Mulk: 8-11]. For this reason they said: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray.﴾ Meaning: the proof was established against us, but we were too wretched to submit to it and follow it, so we went astray from it and were not granted it.

Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.﴾ Meaning: send us back to the worldly abode, and if we return to what we did before, then we are wrongdoers deserving of punishment, just as they said: ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?﴾ [Ghafir: 11]. That is because: ﴿When Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 12]. Meaning: there is no way out, because you used to associate partners with Allah when the believers affirmed His oneness.

This is an answer from Allah, Exalted is He, to the disbelievers when they ask to be taken out of the Fire and returned to this abode (in A: "the world"). He says: ﴿Be silent therein﴾, i.e., remain therein humiliated, abased, and debased. ﴿And do not speak to Me﴾, i.e., do not return to this request of yours, for there is no answer for you with Me.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Be silent therein and do not speak to Me﴾: he said, "This is the saying of the Most Merciful when their speech to Him has ended."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman al-Marwazi narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed the people of Hell will call upon Malik, and he will not answer them for forty years. Then he will respond to them: 'Indeed you will remain.' He said: Their supplication was scorned – by Allah (in F and A: "by Allah, their supplication") – before Malik and the Lord of Malik. Then they will call upon their Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return, we will indeed be wrongdoers﴾. He said: Then He will remain silent toward them for the length of the worldly life twice over, then it will be answered them: ﴿Be silent therein and do not speak to Me.﴾ He said: By Allah, the people did not utter a single word after that, and there was nothing but the groaning (zafir) and sobbing (shahiq) in the Fire of Hell. He said: Their voices were likened to the voices of donkeys, the beginning of it being groaning and the end of it sobbing."

He also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, Abu al-Za'ra' narrated to us, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "When Allah wishes not to bring out any of them – meaning from Hell – He changes their faces and their colors. Then a man from the believers will come and intercede, saying: 'O Lord, O Lord (in F and A: "O Lord, O Lord, O Lord").' He will say: 'Whoever recognizes anyone, let him bring him out.' So the man comes, looks, and does not recognize anyone, and says: 'I am so-and-so.' He says: 'I do not know you.'"

He said: At that point they will say: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return, we will indeed be wrongdoers﴾. At that point He will say: ﴿Be silent therein and do not speak to Me.﴾ When He says that, it is closed over them, and no one from them comes out.

Then He, Exalted is He, said, reminding them of their sins in the world and of their mocking of His believing servants and His allies, saying: ﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants who said, "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful." * But you took them in derision﴾, i.e., you mocked them in their supplication to Me and their humble pleading to Me, ﴿until they made you forget My remembrance﴾, i.e., their hatred for them drove you to forget dealing with Me, ﴿and you used to laugh at them﴾, i.e., at their conduct and their worship, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. ﴿He will say, "You remained but a little, if only you had known."﴾ That is, a short period in any case. ﴿If only you had known﴾ means that you would not have preferred the perishable over the lasting, you would not have conducted yourselves in this evil manner, and you would not have earned Allah's wrath during that brief period. Had you been patient in obeying Allah and worshipping Him, as the believers did, you would have succeeded as they succeeded.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, from Ayfa' ibn 'Abd al-Kala'i, that he heard him addressing the people, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, He will say: 'O people of Paradise, how many years did you remain on the earth?' They will say: 'We remained a day or part of a day.' He will say: 'What a fine profit you made from a day or part of a day: My mercy, My pleasure and My Paradise. Remain therein forever, eternally.' Then He will say: 'O people of the Fire, how many years did you remain on the earth?' They will say: 'We remained a day or part of a day.' He will say: 'What an evil bargain you made in a day or part of a day: My Fire and My wrath. Remain therein forever, eternally.'" [Ibn al-Athir narrated it in Usd al-Ghaba (1/187) with his chain to al-Hakam ibn Musa, from al-Walid, from Safwan, with the same wording.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾ That is, did you suppose that you were created in vain, without any intention or will on your part, and without any wisdom on Our part? ﴿And that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ That is, that you would not return in the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 36], meaning left aimless (hamalan).

* *

As for His words: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the true King﴾ That is, He is far above creating anything in vain, for He is the true King, free from such things. ﴿There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ He mentioned the Throne because it is the ceiling of all creation, and described it as noble, meaning of good appearance and fine form, as He said: ﴿Then We caused to grow therein every noble pair﴾ [Luqman: 10].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman (a shaykh from the people of Iraq) narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Safwan informed us, from a man from the family of Sa'id ibn al-'As, who said: The last sermon that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz delivered was that he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "To proceed: You were not created in vain, nor will you be left neglected. You have a return in which Allah will descend to judge between you and to decide between you. Whoever leaves the mercy of Allah has lost and failed, and is deprived of a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. Do you not know that none will be safe tomorrow except one who has been wary of this day and feared it, who sold the perishable for the lasting, the little for the much, and fear for security? Do you not see that you are from the loins of those who perished, and that after you there will be those who remain, until you are returned to the Best of Inheritors? Then, every day, you accompany a morning-goer and an evening-goer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who has fulfilled his term and whose appointed time has ended, until you bury him in a crack of the earth, in the belly of a crack that is neither level nor provided with a pillow. He has parted from loved ones, mingled with dust, and faced the reckoning, pledged to his deeds, rich in what he left behind and poor in what he sent ahead. So fear Allah, servants of Allah, before the expiry of your covenants and before death descends upon you." Then he placed the edge of his garment over his face, and wept, and made those around him weep.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Yahya ibn Nasr al-Khawlani narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a informed me, from Abu Hubayra, from Hanash ibn 'Abd Allah: that a man who was afflicted passed by 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he recited into his ear this verse: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us? So exalted is Allah, the true King﴾, until he finished the surah, and the man was cured. [This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What did you recite into his ear?" He informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if a certain man recited it upon a mountain, it would move."]

Abu Nu'aym narrated through the route of Khalid ibn Nizar, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent us on an expedition and commanded us to say when we entered the evening and the morning: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ He said: So we recited it, and we gained booty and were safe.

Glory be to Him, exalted above what they associate﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], ﴿In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Hud: 41].'" [al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/124) and in Kitab al-Du'a' (no. 804) through several routes from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hilali, from Nahshal with the same. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/132): "Nahshal ibn Sa'id is abandoned (matruk)."]

Allah, exalted is He, says, threatening the one who associates with Him another and worships someone besides Him alongside Him, and informing that whoever associates with Allah ﴿has no proof for it﴾, meaning he has no evidence for his claim. So He said: ﴿And whoever calls upon another god besides Allah, for which he has no proof﴾. This is a parenthetical clause (jumlah mu'taridah), and the answer to the conditional in His words ﴿then his account is only with his Lord﴾ means: Allah will call him to account for that.

Then He informed: ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾, meaning, in His presence on the Day of Resurrection, there will be no success for them and no salvation.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "What do you worship?" He said: "I worship Allah, and such-and-such," until he counted off idols. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then which of them, when harm befalls you and you call upon it, removes it from you?" He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: ["Then which of them, if you have a need and you call upon it, gives it to you?" He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic."] He said: "Then what leads you to worship these alongside Him?" He said: "I wanted to thank Him by worshipping these alongside Him, or I thought that He might be overcome by them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You know, but they do not know." The man, after he had embraced Islam, said: "I met a man who argued against me."

This is mursal in this chain. However, Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Jami' as a connected report (musnad) from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), something similar to this [Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. 3483, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith."].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And say, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful"﴾, this is a guidance from Allah to this supplication. Ghafr (forgiveness), when used absolutely, means the erasing of sin and concealing it from people, and rahmah (mercy) means that He guides him to be steadfast and makes him successful in his words and deeds.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Mu'minun.
